The Bears are regrouping after a decisive 34-13 road loss to Western Kentucky, while the Owls hope to rebound from a heartbreaking 27-26 defeat at the hands of Jacksonville State. Rickie Collins is the engine for Kennesaw State. picks.blurb: The Kennesaw State Owls (1-4, 0-1 CUSA) won this league last year and were expected to contend for the title again, but they've had a disappointing start to the year and have dropped back-to-back one-score games. Most recently, they lost 27-26 to Jacksonville State in their league opener. The Missouri State Bears (1-4, 0-1 CUSA), meanwhile, were a surprising bowl team last year in their first season at the FBS level. However, with a new coaching staff this season, they've struggled and are still looking for their first FBS win. Can the Hoosiers take down the Buckeyes ? If so, they’ll need most of these predictions to come to fruition. 3 bold predictions for Indiana vs. Ohio State Maryland Terrapins linebacker Daniel Wingate (1) hits Ohio State Buckeyes quarterback Julian Sayin (10) during the NCAA football game at Ohio Stadium in Columbus on Oct. 10, 2026. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect Indiana sacks Julian Sayin five times Indiana sacks Julian Sayin five times In the 2025 regular season, Ohio State quarterback Julian Sayin was sacked six total times in 12 games. Indiana’s defense got to him five times in the Big Ten Championship Game alone. This 2026 matchup should be more of the same – if not an even more dominant showing from the Hoosiers’ pass-rushing attack. Halfway through the regular season, Sayin has already been sacked 11 times. And Indiana has a whopping 20 sacks in six games. The writing is on the wall – in Sharpie. Expect the Hoosiers to apply a lot of pressure on Sayin. It’ll be interesting to see how Sayin responds, especially considering he’s shown off his legs more often this year (and Indiana has been vulnerable to QBs who take off). It has put up at least 31 points in every league game thus far. Sayin and stud wide receiver Jeremiah Smith have been flat-out unstoppable. As for the Hoosiers, they have scored at least 20 in every outing in 2026. Then again, Indiana scored six points through three quarters last Saturday at Nebraska. And, on the flip side, Ohio State hasn’t seen a defense half as sturdy as Indiana’s, aside from Texas, which held the Buckeyes to only three points in the second half. If Indiana’s defense strings together four full quarters, it can bottle up this Ohio State offense – or at least keep it at bay (Smith won’t be entirely shut down by any defense this year). And the expectation is that the Hoosiers offense, which has sputtered at times this year, struggles with this Buckeyes defense. It’d be a surprise to see either team score three touchdowns. Indiana, which is holding opponents to a Big Ten best 75.0 rushing yards per game, has been an absolute brick wall against the run. Noticing a theme? Defense, defense and more of it. Indiana, which is holding opponents to a Big Ten best 75.0 rushing yards per game, has been an absolute brick wall against the run. Ohio State, meanwhile, hasn’t exactly been running through anybody. It managed just 94 rushing yards against Texas in Week 2. Kent State held the Buckeyes to 3.8 yards per carry. You get the idea. In general, Ohio State’s experienced offensive line has been surprisingly uninspiring in 2026. Expect Indiana’s elite defensive front to have its way getting after Sayin and stifling the run game. But can the Hoosiers do enough against Smith? That will be the question. picks.headline: Gators Legend Chris Doering Predicts 'Nasty' Gators vs. No. 7 Longhorns Outcome
picks.blurb: Gators Legend Chris Doering Predicts 'Nasty' Gators vs. No. 7 Longhorns Outcome Skip to main content SI.COM SI.COM GATORS FB SI.COM GATORS BB FOOTBALL FOOTBALL NEWS BASKETBALL NEWS The Florida Gators take on the No. 7 Texas Longhorns on Saturday at Noon EST . The Gators will be eager to return to the field after a pair of less-than-stellar performances the last two weeks. Head coach Jon Sumrall admitted earlier this week that he was taking a more hands-on approach to making sure his players understood what it meant to play Florida Gators football. They'll also be giving second-year quarterback Tramell Jones Jr. his first start after seeing mop-up duty the last two weeks. Gators legend Chris Doering appeared on the Paul Finebaum show to preview the Gators at Longhorns, and he was having flashbacks from the last time Florida traveled to Austin. "For whatever reason, I cannot get the idea or the memory of watching Scott Strickland on the sideline two years ago, last time that Florida went to Austin, and I think they were down 42-0 in the first half and 11:00 a.m. (Central) start," Doering said on the show . Doering was off by a touchdown. It was 35-0 en route to a 49-17 Texas win. However, the kickoff time isn't the only similarity Doering points out. Florida started a backup quarterback two years ago as well. "They were without their starting quarterback. Maybe his mobility can help going up against probably the best front seven that they will face the entire season," Doering said of Jones. Sumrall was unhappy with how the Gators played on the lines of scrimmage in their two losses, and Doering is afraid that won't be fixed quickly enough to beat a powerful Longhorns team. "The blueprint's out on beating Florida. It's being able to out-physical them on the line of scrimmage, being able to stop the run. Everything starts with the run game for Florida. Then the secondary is incredibly porous. Something that we were afraid of in the offseason is now coming to light. "Teams are being able to take advantage of it the last couple of weeks, including last week with LaNorris Sellers converted, I think, about five or six 3rd and 10 pluses." Sellers was an incredibly efficient 23 of 35 passing for 279 yards and four touchdowns in the Gamecocks' 38-19 win. They were 10 for 16 overall on third down. Texas managed 382 yards against Oklahoma last week, but they only scored 24 points in the 27-24 loss to the Sooners. Tennessee held them to 262 yards and 20 points in the previous game. Doering thinks this could be the week the Longhorn offense breaks out. "So, I feel like Texas, if you ever wanted a slump buster, this is it for Texas's offense. I think it's going to get nasty, unfortunately, there in Austin. I think Texas wins by multiple touchdowns," Doering finished. The Longhorns present a big challenge to the Gators, but that also means it's a big opportunity to get back into the College Football Playoff conversation with an upset. The Gators have dropped two straight, including a lopsided defeat to South Carolina, while the Longhorns are looking to regroup after falling to rival Oklahoma and surrendering their No. 1 ranking. Our Florida vs. Texas prediction backs the Longhorns to cover the 10.5-point spread, but our college football expert sees even better value in the game total. Read on for our analysis and more college football picks for Saturday's slate. Who will win Florida vs Texas: Texas -10.5 Have the Florida Gators been "figured out"? I'm not sure. Has Florida had extreme regression over the last few games and probably gotten to a record it should be, even if it required some extremely unbalanced games to do so? Probably so. I'm taking the Texas Longhorns to cover this -10.5 number; it's a small edge, and I wouldn't play it past here. Florida's offense is (still) legit, ranking 8th in EPA per pass, but the defense has been a sieve. The Gators rank 123rd in success rate allowed (49.7%) and dead last at 136th in 3rd/4th down success allowed, so Texas doesn't need to be explosive to sustain drives. They need to be solid, which is pretty much the definition of an Arch Manning-led offense. On the other side, the Longhorns' defense ranks 2nd nationally in adjusted EPA per play, 9th against the run and 11th against the pass, while allowing just 29.9% of available yards (5th) . Florida won't trade scores all afternoon. I'll lay it. TOP PICK Florida vs Texas Over/Under pick: Under 51.5 I'm playing the Under 51.5 and would take it down to 50.5 (50%). It's my top pick. Florida's offense has been efficient, but it hasn't faced a defense that controls early downs as Texas does. The Longhorns rank 5th nationally in early-down EPA per play allowed, which has opponents facing an average 3rd down distance of 8.12 yards , 15th in the country. Florida already ranks 105th in average 3rd down distance at 7.62 yards , so expect a lot of long-yardage situations and stalled drives. Texas also ranks 6th in defensive EPA per drive, so even when the Gators move the ball, points haven't come easily against this unit. The Texas offense isn't built to push this total either. It ranks 55th in success rate and 67th in EPA per pass, and gains just 46.5% of available yards (70th). Expect the Longhorns to win with long, methodical drives that drain the clock rather than quick-strike scores. Florida vs Texas combo This combo is built around one game script: Florida hangs around early, then Texas takes over. Coming off two straight blowouts, the Gators should come out with urgency, and an offense that ranks 8th in EPA per pass can keep them close for a half. Texas's offense isn't built to jump out to fast leads either. The second half is where the Longhorns' advantages show up. Florida's defense ranks dead last in 3rd-and-4th down success allowed, and long Texas drives should wear the Gators down, pull away on the scoreboard, and eat clock to keep this under the total. Florida 1st Half +6.5 Florida vs Texas prop: Florida Under 2.5 touchdowns Florida has been able to move the ball this season, but finishing drives against this Texas defense is a different story. The Longhorns hold opponents to a 38.8% passing success rate (25th) and rank 6th in defensive EPA per drive, so even productive Gators possessions are likely to stall short of the end zone. With Texas expected to control the ball on long drives, Florida's opportunities will be limited, and field goals are the more likely outcome when it does get into scoring range. Coming off a loss, Texas is eager to get back in the conference title picture with a good showing against the reeling Gators. Here's what you need to know heading into the matchup as The Big Lead locks in our final prediction for this Week 7 college football clash. Texas offensive inconsistency and defensive strength Arch Manning has shown flashes but has been uneven against better competition, with turnovers becoming a recurring issue. Pass protection has been mixed despite solid grades in some metrics, and the run game has lacked consistent explosiveness. Where Texas separates itself is on defense. The unit ranks among the better groups nationally in yards allowed and has been especially effective limiting yards after contact. Rushing off the edges and overall tackling efficiency have been strengths. That could create some real problems for a Florida offense that has looked worn down. Defensive collapse, run game issues at Florida NCAA Football: Mississippi at Florida Mandatory Credit: Matt Pendleton-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Even during the Gators' win streak, critics sounded the alarm about this defense. The two-game skid has confirmed those worries. Missed tackles and coverage breakdowns have piled up? The total damage? Florida is the SEC's worst defense in total output, explosive plays allowed, and against the pass. It's the second-worst in scoring. On offense, the Florida run game that once looked dominant has been largely shut down by better fronts. Jadan Baugh's production has dropped sharply. After rushing for over 130 yards in four wins, his totals fell to 13 and then 59 yards in two losses. Questions also linger about quarterback availability with Aaron Philo listed as questionable. A potential shift to Tramell Jones Jr. would add even more uncertainty against a Texas defense that flies to the ball. Key matchup dynamics to watch Texas holds clear edges in defensive structure and home-field stability. Florida's ability to create explosive plays through play-action and yards after catch remains a theoretical strength, but recent film shows those opportunities drying up against disciplined units. Scheme-wise, Texas' ability to limit perimeter runs and finish tackles aligns poorly with what Florida has relied on. Manning should face less pressure than he did against Oklahoma, giving him cleaner looks against a secondary that has been vulnerable. Florida vs. Texas prediction: Who wins and why? Texas is the more complete team right now, particularly on the defensive side of the ball. Even with offensive questions, the Longhorns' ability to control the line of scrimmage and force Florida into obvious passing situations should decide the game. Florida has the talent to keep stretches competitive, but the recent defensive regression and limited run game make a full road upset unlikely. The Big Lead Prediction: Texas 31, Florida 17

Brown coming off IR ALCS Game 4 postponed Defense will win WNBA Finals Alan Youngblood/Gainesville Sun-Imagn Images, Kevin Jairaj-Imagn Images Brandon Little, Craig Smith, Justin Churchill, Rob Gregson, Ryan Roberts, Tyler Forness Thu, October 15, 2026 at 6:48 PM UTC · 5 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads After suffering back-to-back embarrassing losses, can the Florida Gators get back in the win column against a reeling Texas Longhorns team? The Florida Gators are in a rough spot at 4-2 as they head to Austin to take on the Texas Longhorns on Saturday afternoon. After two blowout losses to the Missouri Tigers and South Carolina Gamecocks on homecoming, Jon Sumrall 's team is in a tough spot. They were at one point being talked about as potentially being the 2019 LSU Tigers from on the precipice of collapsing. It's his first year at the helm, and the talent level still isn't quite there yet. For the Longhorns, they have beaten Ohio State, but are coming off a tough loss in the Red River Rivalry to the Oklahoma Sooners. They are in an interesting spot right now, and a win is a must for both teams. Who will get the win? Our experts made their predictions. Texas 38, Florida 24 Can we trust the Florida Gators? Honestly, no, and that includes the four-game winning streak to start the season with a massive blowout win over Ole Miss. The defense is struggling to generate pressure and the coverage on the back end has been incredibly inconsistent. Even with Texas having lost Red River last week, their success so far this season and offensive talent gets the Longhorns the win. Can the Gators get the win? Absolutely! Will they? I doubt it. – Tyler Forness , A to Z Florida Texas 33, Florida 19 Both teams come in off dismal losses to unranked teams. The Longhorns, who haven't looked dominant this year by any means, gagged away a game they should have won against Oklahoma but for a pick six and a punt block touchdown. Florida got mollywhopped by South Carolina one game after getting throttled by Missouri. As such, it's tough to tell up from down with these two teams. But my mind immediately goes to two things. First, the Horns' front is still nasty, and Florida suddenly can't find any space for Jadan Baugh and the ground game. On the other side, Florida's defense has become a sieve, and I don't trust they've found a way to fix it yet. Cam Coleman and Ryan Wingo are too much for the Longhorns, who win comfortably in Austin. – Craig Smith , A to Z Miami Texas 31, Florida 20 Arch Manning has faced plenty of criticism for his inconsistency this season, but this is the type of matchup that could help him get back on track. Florida's pass defense has been a major weakness, and I expect Manning to take full advantage by delivering his best performance of the 2026 season. The Longhorns have the talent to exploit the Gators' struggling secondary, and Manning should find plenty of opportunities to push the ball downfield and put points on the board. After an uneven stretch offensively, this could be the breakthrough performance Texas needs. Florida should have some success early, particularly with running back Jadan Baugh leading the way. Baugh has been one of the Gators' most productive playmakers, and I expect him to help Florida move the ball and keep the game competitive in the first half. However, Texas has the defensive talent to make adjustments and limit Florida's offensive production as the game progresses. The Gators have struggled to maintain consistency in recent weeks, and that issue will catch up with them again in Austin. Texas pulls away in the second half, with Manning and the offense doing enough to secure a much-needed win. – Ryan Roberts , A to Z Notre Dame Texas 21, Florida 17 The Gators have fallen off a bit in the last few weeks after starting red hot. Texas is coming off a disappointing loss to Oklahoma. So, you know, Steve Sarkisian is going to be looking to get his team rolling again. Last week probably showed Texas what they should be doing more often on offense. They need to run more quick-game stuff with Arch Manning, because the long, developing routes downfield aren't helping the offense. Their offensive line isn't great, so they need to start running more quick-game plays. I think this past game showed some of that, and Texas still gets the win despite the offense struggling against a decent Florida defense. – Justin Churchill , A to Z Oklahoma Texas 30, Florida 20 As high as I was on the Florida Gators after the Ole Miss win, that hype has come crashing down after games against Missouri and South Carolina. The offense, led by Jadan Baugh, simply hasn't looked the same, and now the availability of starting QB Aaron Philo is in question. As for Texas, the Longhorns are coming off an embarrassing loss of their own after losing Red River to a bad OU team, and they aim to get back on track. Florida's defense has been bad, to say the least, and this game may serve as a great game for Arch Manning nd Texas. Give me the Longhorns here. – Rob Gregson , A to Z Alabama Texas 28, Florida 17 Texas and Florida both need wins this week, and the pressure is even higher for Steve Sarkisian and Arch Manning. Two losses for Texas at this point in the season would make things very uncomfortable in Austin, and perhaps it would mark the beginning of the end for some important names there. I don't think that's going to happen, though. I think Texas bounces back this week behind a strong defensive performance and looks the part against Florida. If the Longhorns can limit Jaden Baugh, they'll defend home field without much issue. I think Florida hangs around, but the Longhorns put it away in the fourth quarter. – Brandon Little , A to Z Ohio State Final Prediction for Florida vs. Texas It shouldn't be much of a surprise that none of our experts have picked the Gators, as they have lost our trust after the disastrous performances of the last two weeks. A win here would do wonders to get them back in our good graces. This article was originally published on A to Z Sports. away.blurb: DKR-Texas Memorial Stadium is looking for a bounce-back game out of their Longhorns, a team that was stunned by Oklahoma last week. That said, QB Aaron Philo is still listed as questionable, though at this point everyone knows that it'll be Tramell Jones under center in a hostile environment. Jones has gotten a decent chunk of playing time in games already this year, but this'll be his first start, and it comes with a pair of wide receivers still questionable. Vernell Brown III and Bailey Stockton both carry the questionable designation heading into the Week 7 matchup. Florida's lone player ruled out against the Longhorns is running back Duke Clark. When looking at Texas's roster, WR Kaliq Lockett and offensive lineman Jaydon Chatman have both been ruled out. away.blurb: "We'll know more early in the week," Sumrall said. "Not sure how severe yet, but it was substantial enough that he couldn't return today." Graham was on the sideline for the defense's first series, though he remained dressed out, and ultimately returned to the contest near the end of the third quarter, as South Carolina took a 31-13 lead. He finished the game with eight tackles and two sacks. "We had an extended — sometimes weird, but when you have those extended layoffs because it was in the lightning delay, he came back out, and we started the warmup. We came out earlier than normal out of halftime to do our warmup. We usually come out at about six minutes. We came out closer to ten minutes, about nine minutes before we were going to kick to move him just a little bit more with the long layoff. "And just felt a little bit of a cramp. It wasn't substantial. Got a little fluid in him. Came back out and was available. He didn't start the first drive. [ Aaron Chiles ] and [ Jaden Robinson ] started inside linebacker on the first drive, but he was available to go back in pretty quickly. He was back out there before the defense took the field. Sumrall also offered the latest update on Gators slot receiver Vernell Brown III , who missed his second consecutive game after suffering a low-grade knee strain in Florida's Week 4 win over Ole Miss. Brown was ruled out before kickoff after being listed as questionable on UF's availability report daily throughout Week 6. Sumrall suggested Brown was a game-time decision against South Carolina, although the head coach considered it unlikely the sophomore would play based on how his knee felt this morning. "VB was game-time decision-ish. Probably I thought, after yesterday's practice, he participated to some extent. Wasn't fully 100 percent but moved around and did run and took some team reps yesterday. And then just didn't feel like he was capable of doing with confidence as we entered today, this morning. Just wasn't quite confident in cutting it loose. I think he's closer, hopefully. He's cleared to do as much as he can and feels confident in right now," Sumrall said. home.headline: Florida Gators vs. Texas Longhorns: Betting Lines, Injury Report
home.blurb: DKR-Texas Memorial Stadium is looking for a bounce-back game out of their Longhorns, a team that was stunned by Oklahoma last week. Now 4-1 (1-1), this is a huge game for Texas to get back on track against a Gators team that hasn't tasted a conference victory since they upset Auburn on the road and then blew out Ole Miss at the Swamp. That said, QB Aaron Philo is still listed as questionable, though at this point everyone knows that it'll be Tramell Jones under center in a hostile environment. Jones has gotten a decent chunk of playing time in games already this year, but this'll be his first start, and it comes with a pair of wide receivers still questionable. Vernell Brown III and Bailey Stockton both carry the questionable designation heading into the Week 7 matchup. Florida's lone player ruled out against the Longhorns is running back Duke Clark. When looking at Texas's roster, WR Kaliq Lockett and offensive lineman Jaydon Chatman have both been ruled out. Unlike Florida, Texas has a pair of players who are listed as probable, not questionable. Defensive lineman Justus Terry and OL Jordan Coleman make up that list. Florida Gators vs. Texas Longhorns: Betting Lines, Injury Report - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF Florida Gators vs. Texas Longhorns: Betting Lines, Injury Report (IMAGN Images via Reuters Connect) Jordon Lawrenz Sat, October 17, 2026 at 1:28 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads Coming off back-to-back losses, the Florida Gators couldn't have asked for a tougher opponent. Not only do they have to play the No. 7 Texas Longhorns, but this game is taking place in Texas. The biggest story coming into this one is Florida's quarterback situation. How will they look without Aaron Philo? That will be determined in mere hours. According to the SEC Availability Report on Friday, Oct. 16, the Gators are only confirmed to be down one player while Texas will be without two. ESPN Analytics gives Florida just a 12.4% chance to pull off the upset, so that really puts things into perspective. According to DraftKings, Texas opened as 9.5-point favorites, but the odds have shifted to an 11.5-point spread. The Longhorns, to no surprise, are huge money line favorites as they are currently -440 just over two hours before kickoff. Florida sits at +340 in the money line in a game that has an over-under set at 50.5 points. Arch Manning knows he needs a big win after what happened against the Sooners last week, and it's clear many believe that will indeed happen on Saturday, Oct. 17, against these Gators.

With the quarterback situation in flux due to Kamario Taylor's apparent turf toe injury sustained against Alabama, State enters the week as two touchdown underdogs on the first fall-like Saturday of football season. Coaches on both sides have a fair amount of familiarity with each other having worked together in Oxford from 2020-21 as boss and apprentice. If Lebby finds a way to get Taylor healthy and ready to roll on Saturday, this may be a barn burner inside Tiger Stadium based on the talent at the offensive skill positions for each team. However, there is a major statistic that isn't being considered in the equation, and that's Kiffin's putrid record against top-25 opponents: 13-26. Mississippi State enters the weeked ranked No. 16 nationally, according to the Week 7 AP Top 25 poll. With an extra week to lick its wounds and recover from a double-digit loss to Alabama, there's a possibility the Bulldogs can find a way to pull off a stunner and keep LSU out of the College Football Playoff entirely in Year 1 under Kiffin. The Bulldogs come in at No. 11 in the SEC, and No. 27 in ESPN's Football Power Index poll with a projected overall record of 8-4 following a 4-1 start on the season. WIth that familiarity, perhaps both coaches feel they understand each other well with tendencies in play calling. "They're really multiple. Zach [Arnett] was with us for a year [at Ole Miss]," Kiffin said Monday. "After Mississippi State, he came over. He's really smart. It's interesting, because he's running a little of his old defense and he's running (Pete) Golding's defense this year. Now, he's even more multiple." picks.headline: LSU vs. Mississippi State Final Score Predictions: Who Wins and Why?
picks.blurb: LSU vs. Mississippi State Final Score Predictions: Who Wins and Why? Skip to main content SI.COM SI.COM TIGERS FB SI.COM TIGERS BB After LSU traveled to Lexington last weekend, Lane Kiffin and the Tigers are coming off of a disappointing loss, heading into the Week 7 matchup against Mississippi State . LSU heads into the matchup with a recent loss, while the Bulldogs are also traveling to Baton Rouge after a loss to the Crimson Tide in Week 5. Before the No. 22 LSU Tigers host the No. 16 Mississippi State Bulldogs this Saturday, the LSU On SI team predicts which team will win and why. Oct 3, 2026; Baton Rouge, Louisiana, USA; LSU Tigers safety Tamarcus Cooley (0) intercepts a pass from McNeese Cowboys quarterback Jake Strong (not pictured) during the first half at Tiger Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Stephen Lew-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Ross Abboud The time for sloppiness is over, and everyone in LSU’s football program knows it. Ole Miss was a game you could’ve won. Kentucky was a game you should never have lost. That will be LSU’s wake-up call. LSU 48, Mississippi State 24 Brooke Benedict Unlike last weekend's loss to Kentucky, LSU has to get both sides of the ball to play all four quarters, with the defense able to shut down Mississippi State's pass threat, and Sam Leavitt and his receiver options are able to make key plays during possessions. Without any system errors from the offense, defense and special teams, the team will see some much-needed success back at home, being able to win over the Bulldogs and win back their top-ranked reputation. LSU 33, Mississippi State 21 If Mississippi State quarterback Kamario Taylor plays: Kamario Taylor has an incredible ability to control the long ball, which will force LSU's defense to account for that threat almost all of the time, and following the loss to Kentucky, I expect LSU to play a lot more tight man coverage. The LSU offense, clearly more comfortable playing at home, will establish the run with Dilin Jones against the MSST 3-3-5 defense, and LSU will win a close one late in the 4th. LSU 38, Mississippi State 31 If Taylor doesn't play: If Taylor is unavailable in Saturday's game, the MSST backup QB is not a clear answer. Redshirt Freshman Parker Puckett started in place of Taylor against Alabama, but SEC veteran AJ Swann is also a likely option to play. Regardless, I expect the Bulldogs will be less competitive without the SEC TD leader hurling the rock. LSU wins handily at home. LSU 44, Mississippi State 21 Mississippi State Bulldogs quarterback Kamario Taylor (1) waits for the snap during the third quarter against the Alabama Crimson Tide at Davis Wade Stadium at Scott Field. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Adrian Ramirez Adrian Ramirez LSU will bounce back from its overtime loss to Kentucky with a strong performance at home in Tiger Stadium. If both Kamario Taylor and running back Fluff Bothwell miss or are limited by their injuries, I expect LSU’s defense to be too much for Mississippi State to handle. I think the Tigers come out with a point to prove and get to work proving it. LSU 31, Mississippi State 14 Hannah Garcia While there’s the possibility of Taylor and Bothwell being out for the game, the LSU defense is still missing key pieces in Spears and Whit Weeks. The receivers have struggled to find consistency all season with catching the ball and Sam Leavitt’s interception numbers are also something that I think could cause LSU to lose. Mississippi State 24, LSU 17 LSU is desperate to bounce back after a tough loss against Kentucky. The keys to this game are Kamario Taylor’s health and Mississippi State’s secondary. Taylor is one of college football’s best quarterbacks, and if he’s not healthy, LSU’s defensive game plan changes. Meanwhile, the Bulldogs allow the second-most passing yards per game in the SEC, so I expect Lane Kiffin to open up the playbook and attack that weakness. I think the Tigers handle business at home. LSU 35, Mississippi State 21 Published Oct 16, 2026 BROOKE BENEDICT Brooke Benedict is a sophomore at LSU, majoring in journalism. She is originally from Boulder, Colorado, and enjoys skiing, hiking, and Pilates. She's always enjoyed watching sports and the way sports bring people together. She has spent one semester as a sports columnist for the LSU student newspaper, and is am excited to continue her LSU sports reporting career with On SI. (Credit: Stephen Lew-Imagn Images) John Feltman Sat, October 17, 2026 at 12:53 PM UTC · 5 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Mississippi State Bulldogs take on the LSU Tigers in Baton Rouge, Louisiana, on Saturday, Oct. 17. Kickoff is set for 12 p.m. ET on ESPN. LSU is favored by -14 points on the spread with a moneyline of -670. The total is set at 56.5 points. Here's my Mississippi State vs. LSU prediction and college football pick for Saturday, October 17. Mississippi State vs. LSU Pick: LSU -14 (-108) My LSU vs. Mississippi State best bet is on the Tigers to cover the spread. Find the best line available on our live NCAAF odds page and be sure to download the Action Network app for more picks and analysis. Mississippi State vs LSU Odds, Spread, Lines Mississippi State vs LSU Spread : LSU -17.5, Mississippi State +17.5 Mississippi State vs LSU Over/Under : 55.5 Points Mississippi State vs LSU Moneyline : Mississippi State ML +575, LSU ML -850 Mississippi State has been one of the more pleasant surprises in the SEC this season, but I'm not particularly interested in backing the Bulldogs in Death Valley when there's legitimate uncertainty surrounding the most important player on their roster. QB Kamario Taylor is officially questionable with a foot injury , and his availability could completely change the outlook of this matchup. Taylor has been outstanding through five games, completing 66.2% of his passes for 1,450 yards and 17 touchdowns against only four interceptions, while adding another 159 yards and a score on the ground. He's been the engine behind an offense generating +0.22 EPA/Play with a 48.7% success rate, but those numbers become considerably less meaningful if Taylor isn't under center. Taylor initially suffered the injury against Missouri before aggravating it during Mississippi State's 56-23 loss to Alabama, when he was visibly hobbled and eventually exited in the fourth quarter. He was later spotted wearing a protective boot on his right foot. Even if Taylor is cleared to play Saturday, there's a significant difference between being healthy enough to take snaps and being capable of operating Jeff Lebby's offense at full capacity. His mobility is an important component of Mississippi State's offensive identity, and limiting his ability to escape pressure or extend plays could be devastating against an LSU defense that ranks first nationally in EPA/Play allowed. If Taylor can't go, Billy Puckett or AJ Swann would be tasked with replacing one of the SEC's most productive quarterbacks in one of college football's most hostile road environments. That's a massive downgrade, obviously, and it's going to create a massive disadvantage for the Bulldogs' offense. The Bulldogs are also dealing with uncertainty surrounding RB Fluff Bothwell, who's questionable with an ankle injury after leaving the Alabama game early. Bothwell leads Mississippi State with 403 rushing yards and three touchdowns, meaning the Bulldogs could be without both their starting quarterback and leading rusher. That's not exactly ideal when you're heading into Death Valley. LSU is coming off a brutal 35-34 overtime loss to Kentucky, and while I'm not particularly interested in blindly betting on a team because it's supposedly angry, this is a matchup where the Tigers should have significant advantages on both sides of the football. The defensive profile is the biggest reason I'm willing to lay the lumber. LSU is allowing -0.24 EPA/Play, ranking first nationally, and has consistently prevented opposing offenses from sustaining drives. That's particularly important against a Mississippi State offense whose efficiency has been driven largely by Taylor's ability to create explosives through the air and extend plays with his legs. If Taylor is limited, LSU should have considerably more opportunities to generate havoc without sacrificing coverage downfield. The offensive matchup is also juicy, making it a great bounce-back opportunity for Kiffin's team. LSU is averaging 42 points and 524.8 yards per game, including 311 passing yards per contest, while Mississippi State's defense ranks 92nd nationally in EPA/Play allowed. The Bulldogs are also allowing 260 passing yards per game (124th) and just surrendered 56 points to Alabama. That's a defense I'm particularly interested in going up against Lane Kiffin's offense, as there should be ample opportunity for the Tigers to score early and often. Mississippi State will also be without LB Jalen Smith, its second-leading tackler, while LB Zakari Tillman is doubtful. Those absences could create additional problems for a defense that already struggles to consistently get off the field. I'm willing to lay LSU -12.5, and the uncertainty surrounding Taylor is a significant reason why. This number opened around LSU -11.5 before getting bet toward two touchdowns, and I'm much more interested in laying the Tigers below 14 than chasing the move afterward. Mississippi State's offense ranks 25th nationally in EPA/Play, but that efficiency has been built around Taylor's production. We're talking about a quarterback responsible for 18 total touchdowns who's now dealing with a foot injury serious enough to leave his status for Saturday uncertain. Even if he plays, I have serious questions about how effectively he'll be able to operate against an LSU defense allowing -0.24 EPA/Play. If he doesn't, the Bulldogs could be forced to start Puckett or Swann against one of the most efficient defenses in college football. Then there's Bothwell, whose questionable status creates another potential problem for an offense that needs balance to prevent LSU from consistently generating pressure. On the other side, LSU's offense gets a Mississippi State defense ranked 92nd in EPA/Play allowed and 124th in passing yards allowed, with additional injuries at linebacker. That's a pretty significant mismatch. I'm not going to pretend LSU's defense looked particularly impressive against Kentucky, but I'm willing to trust its season-long efficiency profile over one ugly performance. The Tigers should have the offensive advantage regardless of who starts for Mississippi State, and Taylor's injury creates a legitimate possibility that the Bulldogs struggle to keep pace. If Taylor is ruled out, I expect this number to become considerably less attractive. I'll lay it below two touchdowns. Pick: LSU -14

LSU is talented enough to beat anyone, but it's one more loss away from realistically being out of the College Football Playoff. That won't be easy with a brutal schedule over the second half of the season. Mississippi State has had two weeks to get over the 56-23 loss to Alabama. It isn't an easy slate, but at 4-1, it'll still be in the mix for big things if it can get out of Baton Rouge with a win. "Billy (Puckett) and AJ (Swann) obviously are the two guys that have been competing since Day 1 in fall camp and really last spring. So, those guys obviously have the ability to get work if (Taylor) wasn't ready to roll." The first-year starting quarterback exited the Bulldogs' Week 5 game vs. Alabama in the fourth quarter with an apparent injury. He was seen on the ESPN broadcast first walking into the locker room with members of Mississippi State's medical staff. As noted by the Clarion Ledger — part of the USA TODAY Network — Taylor was seen wearing a boot on his right ankle for the remainder of the frame once he returned to the sidelines. Kamario Taylor Isn't Mississippi State's Only Injury Concern at LSU
away.blurb: Mississippi State quarterback Kamario Taylor was listed as questionable for the LSU game on the October 15 report. | Bobak Ha'Eri / Wikimedia Commons (CC BY 3.0) Marvin Uzor Fri, October 16, 2026 at 5:32 PM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads Taylor remained questionable on Thursday's SEC report, the same as Wednesday. Running back Fluff Bothwell also stayed questionable, so the No. 16 Bulldogs (4-1, 2-1 SEC) head to No. 22 LSU (4-2, 1-2) on Saturday at 11 a.m. CT on ESPN with both of their top backfield weapons in limbo. A questionable tag this late leaves more than one possibility. Taylor may still be recovering, or the staff may need more time before deciding how much he can handle. However, the report does not explain why he remains questionable. Bothwell's situation is not far-fetched either. He left the Alabama game after the first drive and finished the afternoon with a boot on his left foot, so redshirt freshman Kolin Wilson and Xavier Gayten could carry a bigger load if he is limited. While the quarterback is busy getting all the major headlines, the defense, on the other hand, took the bigger hit on this report. Linebacker Jalen Smith, who was hurt against Alabama, was ruled out on the first report, and starting linebacker Zakari Tillman joined him on Thursday after playing only once this season. Losing two linebackers against an LSU offense averaging about 42 points per game is a scary thought. Defensive linemen Diesel Moye and Trevion Williams are also out, which thins the front seven even more. The newest names on the report carry less worry. Receiver Anthony Evans III, safety Isaac Smith, and offensive lineman DJ Chester were all added as probable, a designation indicating they are expected to be available. The Tigers equally have their own problems. LSU listed linebacker Whit Weeks and four other players as out, and linebacker Tylen Singleton as doubtful, so both defenses are dealing with absences at Tiger Stadium. home.blurb: Kamario Taylor injury: LSU, Lane Kiffin given layup in CFP chase with star QB doubtful - CBS Sports site: media | arena: collegefootball | pageType: stories | section: | slug: kamario-taylor-injury-mississippi-state-lsu-lane-kiffin-cfp-chase | sport: collegefootball | route: article_single.us | 6-keys: media/spln/collegefootball/reg/free/stories Skip to Main Content Close Menu All Sports Menu Sports Watch Fantasy Betting Featured NFL User Menu Settings Log Out Log In Sign Up Fantasy & Games See All ArrowForward # # LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect With Taylor and star RB Fluff Bothwell doubtful, the Tigers have an unexpected break to revive their playoff hopes before brutal matchups against Alabama, Texas and Tennessee Whether the No. 22 Tigers will play good football when they host No. 16 Mississippi State on Saturday is to be determined, but LSU is undoubtedly beginning the second half of its season with some good fortune. The weather forecast calls for a beautiful fall Saturday, where the high in Athens is supposed to be just 67 degrees. The betting forecast is calling for the Dawgs to beat the Tigers by about three touchdowns. This will likely not be a close game, which means we can be a little looser with our bold predictions for it. Here are three bold ones for Kirby Smart and Alex Golesh’s first game in this rivalry: Georgia has a 100-Yard Rusher and Receiver The Dawgs can take advantage of this Auburn defense, which is a bottom half unit in the conference, allowing over 350 yards of total offense per game. Georgia’s offense has been extremely productive, ranking top three in the conference. Georgia having a back and a wideout go for 100 yards in the same game hasn’t happened in 10 years. So, yeah. This is a bold prediction. I think about a guy like Talyn Taylor or Craig Dandridge, who have hit on some explosive passing plays. All it takes is one or two of those and some screens and underneath throws to work for that 100-yard game to come into play. Auburn is also among the worst rushing defenses in the SEC. We saw Dwight Phillips Jr. run for over 100 yards against Alabama on just 17 carries. He, Nate Frazier and Bo Walker have each registered multiple explosive runs. All it takes is for one of them to bust a huge run and that 100-yard mark is well within reach. Dawgs go for 250 On the Ground Auburn is allowing about 150 yards per game on the ground. I think Georgia could go for over 250. They have done it twice already and ran for over 200 yards in two other games. Auburn allowed almost 250 yards to both Tennessee and Florida. Georgia has a better offense than both of those teams. The Dawgs could really blow Auburn out on Saturday, and if they do that then there will be a lot of yards gained on the ground. Partially due to garbage time. Georgia Holds Auburn to Under 300 Total Yards Auburn has possibly the most unique offense that Georgia will see all year. There is an argument to be made that the Dawgs will struggle more in this game than you would initially think because of that. Auburn takes the least amount of time in between plays and runs more options and designed quarterback run plays than any other offense that Georgia will see this year. I am not buying it. Georgia’s defense has been the best in college football. The Dawgs will shut down Auburn on Saturday. After dominating Alabama physically, the Bulldogs could embarrass the Tigers. The Deep South's Oldest Rivalry returns to Athens this Saturday as No. 1 Georgia (6-0) welcomes Auburn (3-2) to Sanford Stadium for a 3:30 p.m. ET showdown on ESPN. And this matchup could get ugly quickly. Kirby Smart's Bulldogs are coming off an impressive 20-17 road victory over Alabama, while Auburn suffered a disappointing 24-14 loss at Tennessee. Georgia has also won nine consecutive meetings against Auburn, including last year's 20-10 victory in Jordan-Hare Stadium. Georgia: The Bulldogs Are Built DIFFERENT Georgia might have delivered its most impressive performance of the season against Alabama. Despite missing its top two running backs, Nate Frazier and Chauncey Bowens, the Bulldogs rushed for 206 yards against one of the SEC's most talented defenses. Dwight Phillips Jr. stepped up in a major way, while Bo Walker provided additional production in the backfield. Quarterback Gunner Stockton was outstanding, completing 18 of 22 passes for 249 yards while accounting for two touchdowns. Through six games, Stockton has thrown for 1,298 yards and 14 touchdowns, completing more than 76% of his passes. Defensively, Georgia held Alabama quarterback Keelon Russell to just 185 passing yards while recording four sacks. With Chris Cole, Raylen Wilson, KJ Bolden, and Ellis Robinson IV leading the defense, Georgia has the personnel to completely overwhelm Auburn's offense. Auburn: Can the Tigers Even Keep This Competitive? Auburn enters Saturday with serious questions surrounding its offense. Quarterback Byrum Brown has thrown for approximately 1,055 yards with seven touchdowns and seven interceptions. While he's dangerous with his legs, his decision-making has been inconsistent. Against Tennessee, Brown rushed for 107 yards but threw two interceptions in the 24-14 loss. Wide receiver Keshaun Singleton has emerged as a reliable target, recording 29 receptions for 322 yards. However, Auburn's biggest concern might be its inability to consistently stop the run. Tennessee rushed for 237 yards against the Tigers last weekend. That's a terrible sign considering Georgia just rushed for more than 200 yards against Alabama without its top two backs. If Auburn can't contain Georgia's rushing attack, this game could be over by halftime. How Each Team Wins For Georgia, the formula is simple: establish the running game, control the line of scrimmage, and force Brown to beat its defense through the air. Stockton should have plenty of opportunities to attack Auburn's secondary once the Tigers begin loading the box. Defensively, Georgia must contain Brown's mobility and force him into obvious passing situations. For Auburn, everything starts with avoiding turnovers and creating explosive plays. Brown must use his legs to extend drives, while the Tigers' defense needs to generate pressure on Stockton. Auburn cannot afford to fall behind early and become one-dimensional. I don't see this game being particularly competitive. Georgia is coming off an emotional victory over Alabama, but Kirby Smart has built a program that rarely overlooks inferior opponents, especially rivals. The Bulldogs should dominate the line of scrimmage, and I expect another massive rushing performance regardless of whether Frazier and Bowens return. Stockton should have an efficient afternoon, throwing multiple touchdowns while Georgia's defense forces Brown into at least two turnovers. Expect the Bulldogs to establish a commanding lead before halftime and eventually begin rotating younger players into the game. Final Score: No. 1 Georgia 41, Auburn 10 Georgia dominates its oldest rival, improves to 7-0, and continues looking like the team to beat in college football. Final score predictions for Georgia vs. Auburn Rob Gregson, A to Z Alabama : Georgia 30 Auburn 10 After watching the Georgia Bulldogs run all over the SEC's top-ranked rushing defense in Tuscaloosa, Auburn may be in trouble. Truthfully, Georgia is the best team in the country, and Auburn is rebuilding under first-year head coach Alex Golesh. I don't think this team has the explosiveness to score on Georgia, and they certainly don't have the physicality to win the trench battle on either side. Gunner Srockton has also elevated his game this season, making multiple high-leverage throws against Alabama in an extremely tough environment. The Dawgs will roll in this one. Tyler Forness, A to Z Florida : Georgia 45, Auburn 17 I don't see this as much of a game. The Bulldogs are coming off a big win over the Alabama Crimson Tide and showed they can hang with the best in the business. This Auburn Tigers team is in good hands with Alex Golesh, but they aren't there yet. Byrum Brown won't be able to generate much against another great Bulldogs defense. This one will likely be over at halftime. Ryan Roberts, A to Z Notre Dame : Georgia 38, Auburn 14 Georgia looks like the most complete team in the country right now, and I don't see Auburn keeping up for long in this matchup. The Bulldogs have the talent, physicality, and balance to control both sides of the ball, and I expect them to establish dominance early. Gunner Stockton is poised for a big game, taking advantage of Auburn's defense and helping Georgia put points on the board consistently. Once the Bulldogs find their offensive rhythm, the Tigers could struggle to keep this one competitive. The Georgia defense could be just as impressive. Auburn will likely have a few moments, but I don't expect the Tigers to sustain enough offense to seriously threaten the Bulldogs. Georgia can generate pressure, force mistakes, and turn defensive stops into scoring opportunities, letting the lead grow as the game progresses. This matchup highlights just how dangerous Georgia can be when all three phases click. The Bulldogs pull away comfortably and send another message to the country. Craig Smith, A to Z Tennessee : Georgia 44, Auburn 20 Boy, we've kind of forgotten about Gunner Stockton in the big picture, haven't we? The Dawgs' starting quarterback has gotten lost in the shuffle this year, with strong quarterback play from Darian Mensah, Keelon Russell, Kamario Taylor, Josh Hoover, and others. But make no mistake, he executes his team's offense as well as any signal caller in the country, as we saw in Georgia's 20-17 win over Alabama last weekend. More of the same will come on Saturday against an Auburn team that will fight for a half and then find itself out of this by the third quarter. Stockton will continue to impress, running when he needs to and spreading the ball around at a high percentage (18/22 passing last week, with completions by 10 different pass catchers). Georgia might be banged up at RB, but Dwight Phillips Jr.'s 120 yards last week against Bama proved they're basically plug-and-play in the backfield. Justin Churchill, A to Z Oklahoma : Georgia 30, Auburn 10 The Georgia Bulldogs have now proven they are the No. 1 team in the country. Their win over Alabama is about as good as it gets for any team this season, other than maybe Texas beating Ohio State. But, they have to show they can be consistent. And, there are definitely still things to work on. As for Auburn, this offense has not been as fun to watch as we all maybe thought it would in the offseason. But Georgia has the mix of defense and offense that Auburn just simply won't be able to hang around with. Then again, this is a rivalry game, and we've seen some weird things happen in rivalry games this year alone. This article was originally published on A to Z Sports. Heading into this week against Auburn his status was still up in the air even though he hasn't been on the injury report at all this week. These two will be heavily featured again if Frazier isn't able to play, and based on how they did against Alabama that wouldn't be too concerning. Frazier being healthy enough to play solves all of these problems though. This gives Georgia three running backs who have proven themselves this season and a little breathing room in case another injury does occur to their running back room. away.headline: Auburn vs. Georgia early injury report: Who's in, who's out
away.blurb: The Tigers emerge from the bye week relatively healthy, with only two players, tight end Hunter Herring and offensive lineman Tai Buster, ruled out for Saturday's game at Georgia due to injury. However, the biggest news from the initial report is that linebacker Xavier Atkins is officially ruled out. Auburn Tigers — OUT: LB Xavier Atkins, TE Hunter Herring, OL Tai Buster Georgia Bulldogs — OUT: WR Thomas Blackshear, RB Chauncey Bowens, WR Isiah Canion, LB Amaris Williams, S Tyriq Green; Questionable: DB KJ Bolden; Probable: OL Marcus Harrison Atkins, who is tied for the team lead in sacks and second on the team in tackles, has been suspended for Saturday's game at No. 1 Georgia, according to Auburn head coach Alex Golesh. Golesh first mentioned the suspension during Monday's press conference and clarified Wednesday that Atkins is not with the team during practice this week. Golesh will address Atkins' status again next week. The Bulldogs will be without several players, including running back Chauncey Bowens, who leads the team in rushing touchdowns with six. However, Georgia received potentially good news on Wednesday as running back Nate Frazier is not on the availability report after missing four straight games with a rib injury. He was not included on the availability report for Georgia's Week 6 game at Alabama ; however, he did not play. away.headline: Georgia football injury report: KJ Bolden downgraded heading into Auburn game
away.blurb: While offensive lineman Marcus Harrison was removed from the report, Georgia safety KJ Bolden was downgraded from questionable to doubtful. Defensive back Tyriq Green (ankle) — out Outside linebacker Amaris Williams (knee) — out Wide receiver Thomas Blackshear (shoulder) — out Wide receiver Isiah Canion (right leg) — out Running back Chauncey Bowens (lower leg) — out Safety KJ Bolden (right leg) — doubtful Other possibilities include Zion Branch, Ja’Marley Riddle and Blake Stewart. Green would also be worth monitoring but he is out once again after suffering an ankle injury against Western Kentucky. Nate Frazier is once again absent from the availability report for Georgia, indicating he’s able to play. That was the case last week, before Frazier was held out of Georgia’s win over Alabama. Dwight Phillips ran for 120 yards while Bo Walker added another 69 on the ground. But with Bowens and Dante Dowdell both out for Georgia, it will be worth monitoring if Frazier sees the field. Georgia is a nearly three-touchdown favorite against the visiting Auburn Tigers. The Bulldogs also have an off week coming out of this game. The SEC will put out another availability report on Friday, before providing a final update 90 minutes before kickoff. He has 22 tackles, 2 pass breakups, 2.0 tackles for loss and an interception. He led Georgia in snaps played against Alabama. In the event he doesn’t play , Georgia does have options in the secondary. The Bulldogs could slide Rasean Dinkins over and play he and Kyron Jones at safety. Doing so would allow Georgia to keep Khalil Barnes at the star position. The Clemson transfer has excelled in that role for Georgia this season. The Bulldogs have looked like a team that is in store for a long season with how the first six weeks have gone. If they are to accomplish all of their goals this season, it will need Bolden and Frazier healthy and contributing at the end of the season. Saturday’s game is set for a 3:30 p.m. ET start.

away.headline: Georgia Injury Report Ahead of Auburn Game Reveals Troubling Reality with RB Room
away.blurb: As it turns out though, Kirby Smart's team is going to be a little bit banged up as they try to avoid a first home defeat against Auburn in more than two decades. As was the case last week, the running back room is going to be a bit thin. With the reporting around Chauncey Bowens as murky as ever, he has been ruled out for the second straight week and could wind up missing more time than that. Bowens is ruled out along with Isiah Canion, who has not seen much work this season. Thomas Blackshear is also out once again, but this is not a huge surprise. The bigger surprising thing is KJ Bolden being listed as questionable, potentially banged up from the Alabama game but dealing with an unknown injury. Reports from Pete Thamel of ESPN indicated that while Nate Frazier is not on the injury report, he was not last week either but still did not end up playing in the win over Alabama. Regardless, it looks like it could be a significant opportunity once again for guys like Dwight Phillips Jr. and Bo Walker to tote the rock and showcase the depth that Georgia has at the position. Given what the Dawgs proved against the Crimson Tide, they should be able to run the ball with success once again versus Auburn even without Bowens and likely Frazier as well. As Georgia tries to stay undefeated and keep the winning streak against Auburn alive, there is going to be serious urgency from this team to play as well as they did last week, which can often be difficult to replicate. If Gunner Stockton can keep up his strong level of play, this Dawgs team is going to be tough for anyone they face to have a real chance of winning. Once again though, he is going to be doing it with a little bit of a shorthanded running back room. As for what that means moving forward for the rest of the season, it remains to be seen, but Georgia certainly passed the first test with a depleted running back room. Time will tell if they can pass the next one as well.

In George MacIntyre's first start for Josh Heupel, he finished with just a 10.3 QBR in a seven-point win against Arkansas. Following their loss to Georgia a week ago, the Crimson Tide head to Knoxville looking to get back on track. In this classic SEC showdown, I've found a few player props worth dabbling in, including another big outing from Alabama quarterback Keelon Russell. Without further ado, here are my Alabama vs. Tennessee prop picks . Before you get too far, be sure to check out all of our college football picks for Week 7. Best Alabama vs Tennessee props Prop pick #1: Keelon Russell Over 240.5 Pass Yards (53.27%) Alabama star sophomore quarterback Keelon Russell should be amped up to bounce back after an underwhelming 16-for-30, 185-yard performance with just one touchdown in the Crimson Tide's loss to Georgia. That said, it came against arguably the best defense in the country. It was Russell's worst performance since throwing for just 188 yards, one touchdown and two interceptions in Week 2 against Kentucky. Over six games this season, Russell still averages more than this prop at 266.5 passing yards per game. He draws a Tennessee defense that has shut down quarterbacks all season, allowing just 185 passing yards per game. However, what elite quarterback have the Volunteers actually shut down? "Well, they held Arch Manning to just 201 yards." Oh, like that holds up in the year of our Lord 2026. Russell is far better than Manning and has faced far tougher competition this season than what this Volunteers pass defense has seen. Coming off a matchup against one of the country's best defenses, the sophomore should clear 240 passing yards on Saturday. Take this up to 250.5 passing yards. Prop pick #2: DeSean Bishop Over 89.5 Rush Yards (50.74%) With Tennessee's run-heavy offense averaging nearly 43 rushing attempts per game this season, I don't expect that approach to change on Saturday against a very talented Alabama run defense. Over their last three games against Texas, Auburn, and Arkansas, the Volunteers still average 38.33 attempts per game . Tennessee should lean on its leading rusher, DeSean Bishop , to move the ball downfield . Last week against Georgia, this Crimson Tide defense showed some flaws when junior running back Dwight Phillips Jr. rushed for 120 yards on just 17 carries . That's the same number of carries Bishop averages per game this season, and Alabama is coming off a game where it struggled to stop the run. Bishop is averaging 113 yards per game and more than six yards per carry this season. If he gets his usual workload, he should be in a great spot to record 90-plus rushing yards on Saturday. Take this up to 95+ yards. Prop pick #3: Keelon Russell Over 24.5 Rush Yards (53.49%) I gave out this same prop last week, so I'll start this one the same way: If you can secure Russell's longest rush over 15.5 yards , take it! Russell has surpassed that mark in every game this season. Plus, the longest rush prop eliminates the possibility of sacks taking away rushing yards, so if you can access it, take it Over his standard rushing yards prop at 25+. However, Russell has still rushed for Over 25 yards in four of his six games this season . The sophomore quarterback is averaging 7.66 rushing attempts per game, and with the Crimson Tide likely to be leading, as the spread indicates, they'll eventually want to chew some clock. That should give Russell plenty of chances to rack up yards on the ground. The last mobile quarterback Tennessee faced was Auburn's Byrum Brown, who averages 16.2 rushing attempts per game and racked up more than 107 rushing yards against the Volunteers. Russell just needs 25 and should have plenty of opportunities on Saturday. Take this up to 30+ rushing yards. Dijon Lee 's personal foul at the end of the game cost the Crimson Tide a game against their most important rival on the regular-season schedule. Georgia quarterback Gunner Stockton completed a pass to 10 different targets, ending 18-of-22 with six explosives and an average of 10.5 yards per play through the air. Alabama has fallen outside the top 50 in Passing Success Rate allowed, giving up 12 receptions over 30 yards this season. The offense will also look to recover from a passing perspective after quarterback Keelon Russell generated two turnover-worthy plays against the Bulldogs. Head coach Kalen DeBoer had plenty of success on offense against Georgia, averaging 5.8 yards per play, while six of the Tide's nine possessions saw at least two first downs. The Crimson Tide rushing attack ranks top-10 nationally in Success Rate and Line Yards, utilizing inside zone, man blocking and power concepts. Russell hasn't been alone in creating explosives, as running back Daniel Hill averages 3.8 yards after first contact, while Trae'shawn Brown has eight explosives on 51 attempts. After a dip in production due to injury in 2025, wide receiver Ryan Coleman-Williams has returned to elite-level play, producing 2.4 yards per route run on 34 targets. Tennessee snapped a 25-year win drought in Fayetteville with a Week 6 win over Arkansas last week. Quarterback George MacIntyre took over starting duties from true freshman Faizon Brandon, generating mixed numbers for a Tennessee offense that scored 24 points. MacIntyre posted five explosive passes, a touchdown and two turnover-worthy plays. The leader of the offense continues to be the running game with DeSean Bishop , averaging 4.4 yards after first contact with eight rushing touchdowns on the season. New defensive coordinator Jim Knowles has elevated Tennessee's stop unit. No opponent in the first half of the season scored more than 24 points against the Vols. Through three SEC games against Texas , Auburn and Arkansas, the Volunteers are averaging 17 points allowed. Knowles utilized Havoc-minded nickel defenses in previous stops at Oklahoma State and Ohio State , and now Tennessee is producing as well, ranking top-10 in Havoc, Passing Success Rate allowed and coverage grading. The Vols also lead the nation in Passing EPA allowed. The first handicap focuses on how Alabama's defense can stop a run game that features Bishop. Tennessee head coach Josh Heupel's offense is a heavy inside zone team with the offensive linemen in wide splits. The Vols have elected to use an additional tight end this season, running inside zone 59 times in 12 personnel against 49 attempts in 11. Alabama boasts a 47% Success Rate against inside zone when opponents use 12 personnel, a 5% drop from the Success Rate against 11 personnel. The Crimson Tide have allowed ground explosives this season, ranking 65th in Rush EPA allowed. Tennessee must stay in standard downs with Bishop handling the rock, as the Vols own a Success Rate of just 115th in passing downs. The next handicap centers on Knowles' defense looking to limit explosives from Russell and a stable full of explosive weapons for the Tide. Tennessee's shortcomings on defense come against the run, with mediocre ranks in Stuff Rate and Defensive Line Yards. Alabama runs a heavy amount of inside zone, a run concept the Volunteers produce a low 42% Success Rate against. away.blurb: ESPN's Laura Rutledge had previously reported that Coleman-Williams was expected to return to the game with a lower-body injury. Rutledge continued her report that Coleman-Williams came out of the locker room at halftime and went to the medical tent before heading out to the stationary bicycle on the sidelines. Be sure to check out USA TODAY Sports' new College Football Unfiltered podcast , hosted by USA TODAY Sports columnist Blake Toppmeyer. You can stream on YouTube or download via Apple podcasts and Spotify . The 6-foot receiver sustained an apparent lower-body injury late in the second quarter of Alabama's game against the Bulldogs at Bryant-Denny Stadium in Tuscaloosa when he went up for a catch on a second-and-3 pass from Keelon Russell. The Crimson Tide star got another injury scare in the fourth quarter after he took a hit to the head from Georgia defender KJ Bolden. There was no targeting penalty called on Bolden by the officials. He was seen on ESPN's broadcast at the 5:25 mark of the quarter being taken to the Alabama locker room. Coleman-Williams finished the first half with two receptions for 33 yards on five targets before adding his third catch in the second half. His biggest play of the night came on Alabama's final drive of the first half, a 23-yard reception that moved the Crimson Tide into Georgia territory. Alabama capitalized on the opportunity, as EJ Crowell punched in a 1-yard rushing touchdown as time expired to end the half. Here's the latest on Coleman-Williams' injury: Ryan Coleman-Williams injury update Coleman-Williams sustained an apparent lower-body injury in the final seconds of the first half. He later returned after halftime, even catching a pass on an Alabama field goal drive. He does have a slightly noticeable limp as well. Here's a look at the play on which Coleman-Williams was injured in the first half: Later, Coleman-Williams took a hard hit to the helmet on a third-down catch attempt. Bolden hit the talented receiver in the head, though officials declined to call him for targeting. Coleman-Williams exited the game to head to the locker room for an evaluation, Rutledge reported. He left on his own power. What injury does Ryan Coleman-Williams have? Following Alabama's loss to Georgia, Kalen DeBoer told reporters that Coleman-Williams has a head injury. On Monday, Kalen DeBoer updated the statuses of all three of them, with Ryan Coleman-Williams likely to miss some time dealing with a couple of injuries. Here is what head coach Kalen DeBoer said about the three of them during his Monday media availability. "Ryan has a couple of things going on. Worked through an injury to his knee that's been kind of going on, and so we'll deal with that," DeBoer said. "Got the head issue as well. So, we’re gonna address that, even the lower-extremity there this week. Pretty good chance we wouldn’t have him here this weekend. I think he would be probably week-to-week after that." "And then Terrance [Green], just keep evaluating him. This is an injury that’s been going on for a couple weeks now. Just re-aggravated it, and it’s been limiting him in practice. And trying to get him to the game, he, I thought, made a great effort in trying to do that. Just, again, re-aggravated it." DeBoer also circled back on Ryan Coleman-Williams, Josh Ford, and the physicality and toughness that players like those two have shown this season. The Tennessee Vols will host the Alabama Crimson Tide next weekend in Knoxville in a game that's very important for both teams. Tennessee has won the last two matchups in Knoxville against Alabama. Alabama has a big injury concern for the Tennessee game Coleman-Williams suffered multiple injuries in Alabama's loss to Georgia. The junior wide receiver left the game with a knee injury but eventually returned. The bigger concern is the head injury that Coleman-Williams suffered later in the game. Alabama head coach Kalen DeBoer confirmed after the game that Coleman-Williams is dealing with a head injury. Reading between the lines, it's fair to assume that this is a concussion protocol situation. So again, we'll see what information is released this week on the talented wide receiver, but his status for the Tennessee game, at least at this point, is suddenly in doubt. Coleman-Williams had been struggling with drops early in the season (an issue that carried over from last year), but he'd been playing well as of late. Not having him on the field would certainly be a big loss for the Crimson Tide. This article was originally published on A to Z Sports. home.headline: Alabama Injury Blow Hits Before Tennessee Rivalry Showdown
home.blurb: The Alabama Crimson Tide face a tough spot before Saturday's big game against Tennessee. Starting center Racin Delgatty has been downgraded to doubtful, according to Pete Nakos of On3 via Yahoo Sports . This news hurts a team that just lost a close game to Georgia. The team must now rely on sophomore Mal Waldrep Jr. to step into the starting role. Fans in Knoxville will see a loud crowd, and losing an experienced lineman makes that road trip even harder. The injury report changed quickly this week. On Wednesday, Racin Delgatty was listed as questionable. By Thursday evening, Pete Nakos reported that his status had changed to doubtful. This means he will likely miss the game on Saturday, Oct. 17. The team needs every bit of experience they can get on the offensive line. Before the injury news, Alabama had already lost wide receiver Ryan Coleman-Williams. He was ruled out before the Delgatty update came down. Now the team faces two key absences. The offensive line must hold up without its starting center, and the receiving corps is thinner. The team has to find a way to win despite these hurdles. In the simulation, both starting quarterbacks had strong games. Three different receivers had over 100 yards each. The real game will depend on how well the offensive line can protect the quarterback. With Delgatty out, that protection is in question. The numbers from the simulation suggest a high-scoring game, but the injury changes the reality of how Alabama can execute its plan. picks.headline: Ole Miss vs Missouri Predictions: Who Wins Critical Matchup and Why?
picks.blurb: Ole Miss vs Missouri Predictions: Who Wins Critical Matchup and Why? Skip to main content SI.COM FOOTBALL FOOTBALL NEWS BASKETBALL NEWS Somewhat quietly, one of the bigger games on college football slate this weekend is happening at Vaught-Hemingway Stadium between No. 9 Ole Miss (4-1, 2-1 SEC) and No. 13 Missouri (5-1, 2-1 SEC). Both squads enter with one loss and need a win this weekend to maintain a reasonable path to the College Football Playoffs. However, alongside the high-stakes of the matchup are the storylines revolving around each team’s roster. Rebels’ star running back Kewan Lacy will be facing his former team for the first time since leaving Missouri, following his true freshman season in 2024. Meanwhile, former Ole Miss starters Austin Simmons, Cayden Lee and Chris Graves Jr. all return to Oxford for the first time since they entered the transfer portal, following the Rebels’ deep run through last year’s playoffs. Saturday’s kickoff between the Rebels and Tigers is set for 2:30 p.m. CT on the SEC Network. Ole Miss entered the week as six-point home favorites. Ahead of the Rebels' latest pressure-filled matchup, Ole Miss On SI predicts which team wins and why. Sep 26, 2026; Gainesville, Florida, USA; Mississippi Rebels head coach Pete Golding looks on after an interception against the Florida Gators during the second half at Ben Hill Griffin Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Matt Pendleton-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Tyler Komis Welcome to the gauntlet that is the College Football Playoffs….or at least the very real warmup version of it. The loser of this weekend’s game in Oxford isn’t mathematically out of the 12-team race, but it’s going to be a loss that will be immensely hard to overcome looking at Ole Miss’ and Missouri’s schedule. As far as the actual matchup is concerned, going into the game, Missouri has played better on the defensive side of the ball and matches the Rebels’ offensive firepower with Austin Simmons and Jamal Roberts leading the way. The Tigers’ rush attack could have the ability to give the Rebels a long afternoon, and we’ll really find out if Ole Miss improved enough from its nightmare performance defending the run against Florida. Ole Miss doesn’t have to completely shut down Mizzou’s ground game, it more than likely won’t, but if it can limit Roberts and the rest of the production in the backfield, the Rebels should give themselves a real chance at picking up a critical win. In my mind, that’s going to be the key to victory for Ole Miss. I believe this game will come down to the final few possessions and whichever offense has the ball last in that scenario. Given the large sample size we’ve seen of Trinidad Chambliss in those types of situations, I have a hard time picking against those results. Ole Miss 34, Missouri 31 Matt Galatzan All of the talk is going to be about the return of Austin Simmons and Cayden Lee to Oxford, and Kewan Lacy facing off against his former team. However, there needs to be more talk about Missouri's defense, or more specifically, its pass rush. The Tigers have 18 sacks this year, which is tied with Texas for third in the SEC behind LSU and Tennessee. Meanwhile, the Rebels are No. 1 in the SEC in sacks allowed with just five. If the Rebels can protect Trinidad Chambliss and slow down a balanced Missouri offense, they will be in good shape. I think they do both just enough to get the win. Ole Miss 30, Missouri 27 I think Ole Miss will take home a hard-fought victory against former Rebels’ quarterback Austin Simmons, wide receiver Cayden Lee and cornerback Chris Graves Jr. and the rest of the Missouri Tigers. Simmons, Lee and running back Jamal Roberts are likely to give head coach Pete Golding and his defense trouble, leading to a “bend-don’t-break” type of performance, following a bounce-back game against Vanderbilt for the Rebels’ defense. However, I’m comfortable predicting Ole Miss quarterback Trinidad Chambliss, wide receiver Deuce Alexander and running back Kewan Lacy to outplay Simmons, Lee and Roberts and give the Rebels a high-scoring ranked win in Ole Miss’ homecoming game. Ole Miss 38, Missouri 31 Zion Trammell Ole Miss and Missouri feature star-studded quarterbacks in Trinidad Chambliss and Austin Simmons. This has the makings of a high-scoring affair, so whichever quarterback can protect the ball better could decide the outcome. I think Chambliss and Kewan Lacy play their best games of the year, and Ole Miss gets by with a win. Ole Miss 31, Missouri 28 Cooper Ferguson Back in the Vaught, I want to see a great response to the blowout victory in Nashville. All will go well if Trinidad Chambliss plays as he has so far. After a second-half respite in the Vanderbilt game, Kewan Lacy is primed for a breakout game in the 2026 campaign. I fear the talent and connection between Austin Simmons and Cayden Lee, but I do not see the Rebels dropping a game at VHS this season.
