picks.blurb: Rece Davis Predicts Missouri-Ole Miss Winner After Changing His Pick on Air Skip to main content SI.COM TRANSFER PORTAL More from CFB-HQ On SI NEWS Rece Davis expected to be the only voice backing No. 13 Missouri at No. 9 Ole Miss on Saturday, but the College GameDay host changed his prediction after ESPN’s Dan Wetzel and Pete Thamel both took the Tigers first. Davis made his pick on the College GameDay Podcast . He’s forecasting a back-and-forth game in Oxford that ends with the Rebels holding off former Ole Miss quarterback Austin Simmons and the Tigers. Why Rece Davis switched his pick Mississippi Rebels quarterback Trinidad Chambliss (6) hands the ball off to running back Makhi Frazier (25) against the Vanderbilt Commodores | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Davis came into the segment leaning toward Missouri (5-1, 2-1 SEC). That’s the same side ESPN analyst Greg McElroy took earlier this week . Davis came into the segment leaning toward Missouri (5-1, 2-1 SEC). That’s the same side ESPN analyst Greg McElroy took earlier this week . “You guys have surprised me because I thought for sure I was going to be the only one to pick Missouri,” Davis said. “I’m going to change my mind a little bit. Not just because you guys took Missouri, but I was leaning Missouri. Austin Simmons’ revenge, running game, the whole thing.” Davis also pointed to Missouri coach Eli Drinkwitz, saying “a lot of times when Drink hits the mic, sometimes it doesn’t work out as well for the Tigers.” His forecast echoes Sept. 26, when Missouri gave up a fourth-quarter lead in a 31-24 loss at Mississippi State. “A back-and-forth game, up and down. Probably ends up much like Missouri’s last trip to the state of Mississippi,” Davis said. “I’ll say the Rebels hang on. I’ll be the one who says the home team wins it.” Missouri’s top-10 history at stake Missouri head coach Eli Drinkwitz reacts toward a referee during the first quarter against the Mississippi State Bulldogs | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Missouri has rolled since that loss. The Tigers routed No. 8 Florida 45-17 , giving Drinkwitz his first regular-season win over a top-10 team in 11 tries at Missouri, and then beat Texas A&M 27-6. Missouri has rolled since that loss. The Tigers routed No. 8 Florida 45-17 , giving Drinkwitz his first regular-season win over a top-10 team in 11 tries at Missouri, and then beat Texas A&M 27-6. “If Missouri can do it, having a top-10 win because the Gators were top 10 at the time, they can win multiple games against top-10 teams for the first time since 1978,” Davis said. That 1978 team shut out defending national champion Notre Dame 3-0 and beat No. 2 Nebraska 35-31. Simmons lost Ole Miss’ starting job after a Week 2 ankle injury against Kentucky in 2025. At Missouri, the left-hander has thrown for 1,434 yards, 14 touchdowns and one interception, which is one yard fewer than Trinidad Chambliss has for the Rebels. Tigers running back Jamal Roberts leads the SEC in rushing. He’ll face an Ole Miss run defense that ranks last in the conference at 176.4 yards allowed per game and 106th nationally in EPA per rush allowed . “The Ole Miss defense hasn’t been what we thought it was going to be,” Davis said. “I remember talking to some people in the preseason, thinking this might be one of the best defensive fronts in college football. Maybe it’ll turn out to be, but so far we haven’t seen evidence of that.” How can Ole Miss hang on? Ole Miss (4-1, 2-1 SEC) counters with Chambliss, a Heisman Trophy contender who’s back for another season after he won an injunction against the NCAA , and running back Kewan Lacy, who began his career at Missouri. “There’s also a little bit at stake here in the personal rivalry for Trinidad Chambliss, too. Maybe Kewan Lacy,” Davis said. Lacy set Ole Miss’ single-season record with 1,567 rushing yards in 2025 and signed a deal to return to Oxford . Still, his health hangs over this week. A shoulder injury kept him out of the 52-28 loss at Florida, and he left last week’s 52-17 win at Vanderbilt after seven carries. The Rebels’ offense ranks eighth nationally in success rate, while Missouri’s defense has allowed 23 points total across its last two games. Kickoff is 3:30 p.m. ET on SEC Network, and the loser falls to 2-2 in SEC play. Can the Tigers pull off another upset, or will the Rebels defend Oxford? Two of the SEC's most intriguing teams are set to collide Saturday afternoon as No. 13 Missouri (5-1) travels to Oxford to face No. 9 Ole Miss (4-1). Both programs are coming off dominant victories. Missouri dismantled Texas A&M 27-6, while Ole Miss embarrassed Vanderbilt 52-17. With both teams sitting at 2-1 in conference play, Saturday's matchup could have major implications for the SEC Championship race and College Football Playoff. Missouri: The Tigers Are Legitimate Contenders Eli Drinkwitz has Missouri playing some outstanding football, particularly on defense. The Tigers are allowing just 17.7 points per game and rank eighth nationally in rushing defense, surrendering approximately 78 yards per contest. Offensively, former Ole Miss quarterback Austin Simmons has thrown for 1,434 yards, 14 touchdowns, and just one interception. Now, he gets an opportunity to prove himself against his former program. But Missouri's biggest weapon has been running back Jamal Roberts. Roberts has rushed for 828 yards and eight touchdowns, including consecutive 200-yard performances. Against an Ole Miss defense allowing 176.4 rushing yards per game, he could be in for another massive afternoon. Former Ole Miss wide receiver Cayden Lee has also been outstanding, recording 42 receptions for 616 yards and five touchdowns. If Missouri establishes its rushing attack early, the Tigers could control this game. Ole Miss: Can Trinidad Chambliss Carry the Rebels? Pete Golding has Ole Miss back in the national conversation following last season's historic playoff run. Quarterback Trinidad Chambliss continues to be one of the most exciting players in college football, throwing for 1,435 yards and 11 touchdowns through five games. Wide receiver Deuce Alexander has emerged as his favorite target, recording 32 receptions for 503 yards and five touchdowns. The Rebels are averaging 38.8 points and nearly 434 yards per game, but their defense remains a major concern. Ole Miss is allowing 28 points per game, including an embarrassing 52-point performance against Florida earlier this season. And facing Missouri's balanced offense certainly won't make things easier. However, the Rebels have been outstanding at home, winning all three of their games in Oxford this season. How Each Team Wins Missouri must establish Roberts early and force Ole Miss into a physical, defensive battle. If the Tigers can dominate time of possession and limit explosive plays from Chambliss, they have an excellent opportunity to leave Oxford with a victory. For Ole Miss, everything starts with its passing attack. Missouri's defense has been elite against the run, meaning Chambliss will likely need to carry the offense. The Rebels must also force Simmons into mistakes and prevent Roberts from consistently reaching the second level. This matchup has all the ingredients for one of the best SEC games of the weekend. Missouri's rushing attack should give the Rebels serious problems, and I expect Roberts to surpass 100 yards once again. However, I trust Chambliss and the Ole Miss offense to deliver when it matters most. The Rebels' explosive passing attack, combined with a sold-out Vaught-Hemingway Stadium, should be enough to overcome Missouri's physicality. Expect a back-and-forth contest that comes down to the final minutes, with Chambliss engineering a late scoring drive to secure the victory. Brown coming off IR ALCS Game 4 postponed Defense will win WNBA Finals Story by Columbia Daily Tribune Missouri football at Ole Miss scouting report, score prediction for top-15 game Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Top-15 matchup. Significant implications for the College Football Playoff. Over to Oxford, where either Mizzou or Ole Miss will finish Week 7 in a strong position to make a run in the second half of the 2026 regular season. No. 13-ranked Missouri football will face No. 10/9 Mississippi on Saturday, Oct. 17, in a Week 7 SEC matchup at Vaught-Hemingway Stadium in Oxford, Mississippi. Like Eli Drinkwitz ended his midweek press conference, "look forward to seeing you on the SEC Network," with kickoff for the top-15 game set for 2:30 p.m. CT. The Tigers (5-1, 2-1 SEC) have won back-to-back league games over Florida and Texas A&M by multiple touchdowns. Mizzou's only loss so far this year was against the other half of the Egg Bowl, dropping a one-score game to Mississippi State in Starkville. Ole Miss (4-1, 2-1) bounced back from a loss to Florida with a blowout win over Vanderbilt this past Saturday in Nashville, Tennessee. Here's what Mizzou fans need to know about the Rebels, from their starting quarterback to their top playmakers, as well as a score prediction for the Week 7 game: Mizzou has 3 players from Ole Miss CFP roster, including QB Austin Simmons Anyone with a passing interest is aware: Austin Simmons is among three MU players going back to face their former team, along with wide receiver Cayden Lee and cornerback Chris Graves Jr. Simmons' situation is a little different. He's going to duke it out against the quarterback who took his starting job last season. Trinidad Chambliss was one of the stories of the season in 2025, leading Ole Miss to the College Football Playoff semifinals in his first season after transferring up from Division-II Ferris State. But the thing with Cinderella tales in sports … someone has to lose. That was Simmons, who began last year as the Rebels' starter. He's been widely praised in Oxford for how he handled the change and, essentially, a benching. He sustained an ankle injury in Week 2 and never got his job back. All's well that ends well. Simmons has found new life as the starter at Missouri and is beginning to generate some first-round NFL Draft interest. Chambliss is back in college because of an offseason court case that revolved around a medical redshirt during his time at Ferris State. Mizzou has a tough job defending Chambliss, who is currently fourth in the betting odds for the Heisman Trophy. He's mobile, has a tremendous arm and doesn't take too many sacks. Missouri has a dangerous offense, too, with Simmons and Lee leading the group. The winner is rewarded with a clearer path to making the CFP this year. "I wish them a lot of luck," Ole Miss coach Pete Golding said Oct. 12, "other than this week when we're playing against them." More: Missouri football's biggest test yet comes in star Trinidad Chambliss More: Why Eli Drinkwitz isn't concerned with Ole Miss' familiarity with Austin Simmons How much does Kewan Lacy elevate Ole Miss offense? Speaking of reunions … Kewan Lacy started his career at Mizzou in 2024. He was a reserve behind Nate Noel and Marcus Carroll. He transferred to Ole Miss after his rookie year, which — talk about sliding doors moments — was among the reasons the Tigers added Ahmad Hardy out of the portal. Hardy and Lacy were Nos. 1 and 2 in the SEC for rushing yards last year, respectively, so the move worked out just fine for all parties. It'll be Lacy vs. Jamal Roberts on Saturday out of the backfield. Roberts currently leads the Power-conferences with 828 rushing yards. Lacy has been dealing with a shoulder injury and missed much of the start of this season. He returned this past Saturday in Ole Miss's win at Vandy with seven carries for 39 yards and a touchdown. Ole Miss's running numbers on the box score are modest, but the analytics paint a much prettier picture. The Rebels' rushing success rate of 60.7% ranks 10th nationally, per Hudl IQ. Every time they run the ball, they're generating 0.16 in 'Expected Points Added,' which is in the top five in the SEC (Missouri's EPA per rush is 0.05). A fully healthy Lacy can only help that cause. He forced 89 missed tackles last season, a number only bested by Hardy. He led the nation with 24 touchdowns. Sep 19, 2026; Oxford, Mississippi, USA; Mississippi Rebels running back Kewan Lacy (5) carries the ball against the Louisiana State Tigers during the first quarter at Vaught-Hemingway Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Petre Thomas-Imagn Images Ole Miss run defense has struggled So, Ole Miss's offense looks pretty good. The defense, however … The Rebels are allowing 392.4 yards per game, which is the second-most in the SEC. The kicker — Ole Miss is giving up 176.4 yards per game on the ground. That's the worst in the conference by quite some distance. Opponents' rushing success rate against Ole Miss is above 50%, per Hudl IQ, which means offenses are staying on schedule with more than half of their rushing attempts against the Rebels. Only Florida, which Mizzou gashed for 220 yards on the ground, Arkansas and Vanderbilt have defended the run worse in the SEC. Teams are generating runs of 15 or more yards 5.6% of the time against Ole Miss and runs of 30 or more yards 3.1% of the time. The Rebels have given up explosives. Roberts just became the third running back in the SEC in the last 20 years to run for 200 or more yards in back-to-back FBS games. The Tigers are committed to the run game, and unless Ole Miss has found a week-to-week fix, they should find some opportunities for Roberts to get loose. Missouri Tigers running back Jamal Roberts (20) celebrates with offensive lineman Tristan Wilson (73) after scoring against the Texas A&M Aggies during the second half of the game at Faurot Field at Memorial Stadium on Oct. 10, 2026. Score prediction: Missouri 41, Ole Miss 38 When I wrote a game-by-game prediction on Aug. 29 before the season, I wrote the following about Mizzou's trip to Ole Miss: "Something about this game just feels like it's going to get weird. Break containment." I have not moved off of that prediction. My chaos radar is going berserk. I am, however, changing who I think will win. Ole Miss does not seem particularly adept at stopping the run. Roberts is not the back you want to see when you're struggling to contain chunk plays. The outside zone and fist fight it creates is not the scheme you want to work out the problems against. Mizzou's defense has been tremendous, but Ole Miss is going to score. The Rebels are too good not to. Our pregame prediction just has Missouri scoring more. away.headline: Ahmad Hardy injury update: Star Missouri football RB not yet back in practice
away.blurb: Missouri head coach Eli Drinkwitz said that there currently is no change to the Mizzou football running back’s injury status during his press availability Tuesday, Oct. 13. Drinkwitz said that Hardy has not yet started a two-week ramp-up period that he needs to see for the running back to return to the field. Drinkwitz, as recently as last Tuesday, said that he’d provide an update as soon as one was available. But rumors began to swirl on various online platforms Monday night, including PowerMizzou at 247Sports and on Reddit, that Hardy may be close to a return to practice. Drinkwitz was again asked about Hardy’s current status on Tuesday. The message board poster has become quite popular for a string of Mizzou predictions over the past year, some of which have panned out. “If he practices, I promise, I'll tweet it out. I won't even give it to Pete (ESPN reporter Pete Thamel),” Drinkwitz said. “We'll just do it ourselves. So, again, I think it's going to be really important — I know everybody's excited about where we're at and all that good stuff. When he's available, I promise you we’ll be excited to use him. But that’s not the story right now. So, nothing new.” Mizzou has its idle week after the game against the Rebels. That technically means that if Hardy is able to return to practice sometime this week, he would be in a position to possibly return for Mizzou’s next game Oct. 31 at Arkansas. (Photo by Chris Leduc/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Cameron Underwood Fri, October 16, 2026 at 11:18 PM UTC · 5 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Welcome back! In case you missed it, Saturday's rivalry game between the Miami Hurricanes and Florida State Seminoles is on deck, and we're here to share our predictions for the game. Call your shot. How does Canes vs Noles play out, who wins, and what's the score? Cam Underwood: Miami is clearly the superior team and superior program, and that's going to play out on the field. Miami is bigger, faster (save Danzy), stronger, and just flat out better than FSU. The spread opened with Miami as 3 touchdown favorites, and that's probably conservative to be honest. Miami wasn't even favored by this much when they beat FSU by 6 touchdowns in 2020. This should reasonably be a repeat of that kind of score line. This one won't be close, and I'm not going to let the colors of the jerseys sway me from that thought. This will be an epic asskicking and I'm going to enjoy every moment of it. Miami 55 Florida State 10 Justin Dottavio: THROW OUT THE RECORD BOOKS!!! As the Solid Verbal says. If I'm FSU and Mike Norvell I'm going to pull out every last stop. He likes trick plays, be aware of the onside kicks, fake punts, fake FG's, double reverse passes etc. Do I think that works? No. I think Miami should dominate the FSU I saw on tape from the Louisville game. But it is a rivalry game and it could have tricky aspects. Miami has been banged up but a bye week prior to the FSU game was a perfect placement. I think Miami wins this by 17+ and it could get ugly if the 'Noles quit. If I have to pick a final score it's Miami 45 FSU 20. Craig T. Smith: It's Miami and Florida State, and that always gives me pause about a blowout. Even the last two years, where Miami was light years better than FSU, there were moments where this game was closer than it should have been. And then, I went and checked the yardage that Florida State's defense has allowed this year. SMU, Alabama, and Louisville all went for well over 500 years each. Uh oh. Miami is the best offense and team that the Seminoles will face this year. Darian Mensah is on one right now, and Miami's offensive line has found its groove lately in run blocking. The Canes' defense also will have two starters back in Marquise Lightfoot and Xavier Lucas. This one is going to get ugly after all, folks. Miami 52, Florida State 23 Mike Schiffman: I am always fearful of a jinx. But not this year. I do think the 'Noles will come out swinging and have some success on a few scripted plays. Beyond that, I don't see them doing much on offense, especially with Xavier Lucas returning to cover FSU wide receiver Duce Robinson. On the other side of the ball, Miami is too creative with too much talent. Mensah and Co. will get their points. If the weather is bad, that could slow down the scoring some, but not enough. Miami 38, Florida state 10 Jake Marcus: The injury bug has hovered over Miami all season, but the bye week came at exactly the right time (although this season will likely be themed "next man up"). Xavier Lucas, Damari Brown, Marquise Lightfoot, and Ezekiel Marcelin are expected back, and the Canes enter rivalry night as the nation's top scoring offense (49.6 PPG) and top scoring defense (9.8 PPG allowed) – that's pretty damn good. Florida State comes in 3-3 after a 44-20 loss at Louisville, where it gave up 397 rushing yards even after a promising start out of the gates. Duce Robinson is the one player on the Noles' side who can flip a game. The 6-foot-6 senior caught 1,081 yards last year and led the ACC in contested-catch rate, but he's been relatively quiet this fall (17 catches, 294 yards through six games). He's still the lone matchup problem, but he'll face a secondary that's finally closer to full strength. Rain and thunderstorms are very likely at Hard Rock Stadium on Saturday night, which could mean a sloppy, turnover-prone game and might nudge FSU toward leaning on Ashton Daniels and its run game. While sometimes weather and rivalry aspects can play 'equalizer', the wet conditions only shrink the margin for the team with the thinner roster and that's not close here. I like Miami's front to win early, and Darian Mensah doesn't need perfect weather to build a first-half cushion. By the fourth quarter the Canes will be sending in the backups, and the calls for Mike Norvell's job will only get louder heading into FSU's bye. Miami 41, Florida State 6 . Rob Weaver: This Saturday night the Florida State Seminoles will quite literally subject themselves to a storm. Only once this season – a dimly lit affair to open the season – have the Seminoles not scored at least 34 points. FSU running back Ousmane Kromah is one of only two ACC backs to have rushed 100 times this season, and he's maintaining a very respectable 5.7 yds per carry. WR Duce Robinson is a preseason all-conference selection. The weapons are there for FSU. And yet, the Hurricanes' unequivocally best defense in the conference (just 249 yds and 9.8 pts allowed per game) are returning multiple contributors from injury. Darrian Mensah and crew will get theirs, but the hallmark of this game will be the Hurricanes defense outclassing FSU unlike Alabama, Louisville, or any other of FSU's opponents. Miami 38, Florida State 13 There you have it. Our predictions for Canes vs Seminoles. How do YOU see the game playing out? Hop in the comments and share your thoughts.

Can the struggling Seminoles avoid another embarrassing defeat? One of college football's fiercest rivalries returns as No. 3 Miami (5-0) hosts Florida State (3-3) at Hard Rock Stadium. These two programs couldn't be heading in more different directions. Miami is coming off a dominant 41-13 victory over Clemson and remains firmly in the national championship conversation. Meanwhile, Florida State suffered an embarrassing 44-20 loss to Louisville after blowing an early 14-0 lead. With Miami entering as a heavy favorite, Mike Norvell and the Seminoles could be in serious trouble. Miami: The Hurricanes Look UNSTOPPABLE Mario Cristobal has built one of the most complete teams in college football, and quarterback Darian Mensah is playing like a legitimate Heisman Trophy contender. Mensah has thrown for 1,438 yards, 15 touchdowns, and zero interceptions this season. Miami is averaging an incredible 49.6 points per game while allowing just 9.8. Freshman sensation Malachi Toney has been nearly impossible to defend, recording 604 receiving yards and six touchdowns. His explosiveness gives Miami a dangerous weapon against a Florida State secondary that has struggled against quality competition. Running back Mark Fletcher Jr. provides another dimension to the offense, and Miami should have opportunities to establish the run against a vulnerable Seminoles defense. Florida State: Mike Norvell Is Running Out of Answers Florida State's season has quickly become a disappointment. The Seminoles allowed an unbelievable 397 rushing yards against Louisville, including 235 yards from Isaac Brown. That's a massive problem against Miami's balanced offense. Quarterback Ashton Daniels has thrown for 1,320 yards, eight touchdowns, and seven interceptions this season. Although Daniels has been dangerous with his legs, his inconsistency as a passer could become a serious issue against Miami's defense. Running back Ousmane Kromah has been productive with 565 rushing yards, but the Seminoles cannot rely entirely on their ground game if Miami builds an early lead. Florida State has enough athleticism to make some plays, but its defensive struggles and offensive turnovers make this an extremely difficult matchup. How Each Team Wins For Miami, the formula is simple: establish the run, protect the football, and allow Mensah to attack Florida State's secondary. Defensively, the Hurricanes must contain Daniels' rushing ability and force him to win from the pocket. For Florida State, everything starts with controlling possession. The Seminoles must establish Kromah, limit Miami's explosive plays, and create turnovers. If Florida State allows this game to become a shootout, it could get ugly quickly. I simply don't see Florida State having enough answers for Miami's offense. Mensah has been outstanding, and I expect him to continue his Heisman-caliber season against a Seminoles defense that just surrendered 44 points to Louisville. Florida State should create a few explosive plays with Daniels and Kromah, especially early, but Miami's defense will eventually take control. I expect the Hurricanes to establish a comfortable halftime lead before completely taking over in the second half. Final Score: No. 3 Miami 45, Florida State 20 Miami remains undefeated, improves to 6-0, and strengthens its national championship case. Defensive coordinator Corey Hetherman has a fair amount of experience in facing dual-threat quarterbacks and finding success. The Hurricanes have the highest-scoring offense (averaging 49.6 points) in FBS; meanwhile, the Seminoles have the 20th worst total defense. Oklahoma just knocked off previously unbeaten Texas, 27-24, and while quarterback John Mateer and the offense continue to be inconsistent, the Sooners' defense has been considerably more trustworthy. That's exactly why I'm attacking Kentucky's team total rather than laying the points with the Sooners. Oklahoma ranks inside the top 15 nationally in both total defense and passing yards allowed, as head coach Brent Venables has built a unit capable of generating pressure without consistently exposing its secondary. That becomes a difficult matchup for Minchey, particularly if Baxter is limited or unavailable. Kentucky's offense has shown it can generate explosives, but the Sooners have done an excellent job forcing opponents to string together multiple successful plays rather than giving up cheap touchdowns. That's the type of defensive profile I want when betting a team total under. This defense is nasty. Oklahoma's offense also has enough uncertainty of its own, which is another reason why I'm not particularly interested in trusting the Sooners to cover a substantial number. Mateer has thrown eight touchdowns against four interceptions, and the offense has been inconsistent enough that Oklahoma could win this game comfortably without necessarily putting up a massive score. You can't trust this Oklahoma offense even in a plus matchup, but you can put faith in its defense. Expect the Sooners to stifle the 'Cats all afternoon and win an ugly one. This is a pretty straightforward sell-high spot, and you could argue it could be a letdown for both teams. Expect both sides to come out flat, but one thing is certain: Oklahoma's defense is the best unit on the field. Kentucky just knocked off a top-10 LSU team in an emotional overtime thriller, while Oklahoma is coming off a massive rivalry victory over Texas. The Wildcats' 35 points against Blake Baker's Tigers defense are impressive, but they benefited from several high-leverage plays and an overtime touchdown, which isn't the type of scoring environment I'm expecting in Norman. Oklahoma's defense ranks among the country's best in limiting passing production, and if the Sooners can consistently force Minchey into second-and-long situations, I think Kentucky will struggle to generate enough successful plays to sustain scoring drives. The Baxter injury is also worth monitoring because Kentucky needs its rushing attack to remain efficient against Venables' front. If the Wildcats can't establish the ground game, the Sooners should have opportunities to generate Havoc and force punts rather than allowing Kentucky to consistently reach scoring position. Don't be concerned with whether or not Oklahoma covers the full-game spread , but its defense will stifle the 'Cats all afternoon. The Sooners could win 24-13, 27-10 or even 20-14, and all three outcomes cash our ticket. Sell Kentucky's offensive performance against LSU, and trust Venables' defense at home. picks.headline: Oklahoma offense preview: Can Kentucky keep the Sooners struggling

Brown coming off IR ALCS Game 4 postponed Defense will win WNBA Finals Story by Wildcats Wire Oklahoma offense preview: Can Kentucky keep the Sooners struggling Braxton Howard, UK Wildcats Wire Wed, October 14, 2026 at 4:11 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Kentucky football travels down to Norman to face the Oklahoma Sooners on Saturday, and both of these teams have plenty of momentum coming into this matchup. Arguably no team in the country has more momentum on their side than the Wildcats right now, coming off back-to-back walk off two-point conversions for the win in overtime. However, Oklahoma came off of their bye week and got a massive win over Texas in the Red River Rivalry game. With that being said, do not let the final score fool you, Oklahoma is still really struggling on offense. Oklahoma's offense will be the worst unit on the field this Saturday, and despite a big 27-24 win over Texas, the issues have not been fixed. The Sooners have scored just six offensive touchdowns since week two. They have only scored over 20 points twice this season, this was week one against UTEP and against Texas where they needed a blocked punt for a touchdown and a pick six to do so. This is a night game in Norman and will present a lot of adversity for Kentucky. The matchup to watch is the Kentucky offense versus the Oklahoma defense, but we will get into that side later. Basically every single offensive metric that you look at to determine offensive success, the Sooners rank bottom five in the SEC. Oklahoma ranks dead last in the conference in all of these statistics: Success rate, Rush SR%, EPA per rush, Explosive play rate and 1D+TD%. They also rank bottom five in the SEC in these statistics: EPA per play, EPA per dropback, Pass SR%, 3rd Down conversion rate, Early Down conversion rate and yards per play. This might be the worst offense Kentucky faces this season unless they can turn things around quickly. Oklahoma ranks first in the SEC in three-and-out rate and negative play percentage. The Sooners have the worst yards per carry average in the FBS. This is a stark contrast because Kentucky's defense ranks top five in the SEC in explosive % allowed and negative % forced. Kentucky's defense has excelled at three things this season: forcing turnovers, forcing negative plays and limiting explosives. This Oklahoma offense has struggled, but they do have some playmakers. The number one guy that should scare you, ironically, is number one Isaiah Sategna. Sategna is a dynamic receiver who is the one guy that can consistently create separation and he is dangerous with the football in his hands. Kentucky has to know where Sategna is on every snap because he is lightning in a bottle when he gets his hands on the football. John Mateer is a reckless but talented quarterback, he made the best throw of his season against Texas to set up the Sooners for the game winning field goal. Mateer threw a perfect back shoulder to Sategna from the far hash. Mateer has arm talent and is a dangerous runner, he immediately looks to run when a pass play breaks down. However, Mateer is extremely turnover prone, even moreso than LSU quarterback Sam Leavitt. Kentucky forced two turnovers on Leavitt, and they need to repeat that on Saturday. They have done a great job of forcing turnovers all season, they did it against Keelon Russell, Marcel Reed, LaNorris Sellers and Leavitt. This defensive line has to get pressure on Mateer to force him to play recklessly. The Wildcats have struggled with scrambling quarterbacks this season, but they were better last week against Leavitt--same thing applies this week with Mateer. Oklahoma as we stated, averages the fewest yards per carry in all of FBS. This is a game where Kentucky should be able to make Oklahoma one dimensional, which is a massive advantage for the Wildcats. The defense has to make Mateer uncomfortable in the pocket and they will have a great chance to win this football game. Kentucky's defense has the opportunity to have their best performance of the season this Saturday. What a wild Saturday it was for the Kentucky Football team. The Wildcats escaped with a 35-34 overtime victory over then-No. 10 LSU Tigers inside Kroger Field while rocking the iconic Power K jerseys. The game featured plenty of twists and turns, including trick plays that resulted in LSU touchdowns, explosive plays from Kentucky’s offense and special teams, turnovers, and, most importantly, missed field goals. Through it all, Kentucky remained competitive. With LSU facing a fourth-down situation late in regulation, the Tigers elected to punt rather than go for it. Kentucky then drove down the field in less than two minutes, setting up kicker Adam Zouagui for a field goal to send the game into overtime after he had missed his previous two attempts. Kentucky won the coin toss and elected to play defense first. LSU quickly drove down the field and scored a touchdown. The Wildcats then got their opportunity, and on third-and-10, quarterback Kenny Minchey connected with Kenny Darby, who nearly took the ball into the end zone but came up a yard short. CJ Baxter immediately punched it in for a touchdown, leaving Kentucky down by one point. Instead of kicking the extra point to force a second overtime, first-year head coach Will Stein decided to go for the two-point conversion to win the game. The decision paid off. Minchey called his own number on a quarterback draw, found plenty of open space, and crossed the goal line untouched to secure the victory. Kentucky defeated LSU 35-34 in overtime, improving to 5-1 overall and 3-1 in SEC play. The Wildcats are now ranked No. 15 in the AP Top 25 poll. Oklahoma Sooners (3-2, 1-1 in SEC) The Oklahoma Sooners have faced increased scrutiny this season after finishing the 2025 campaign with a 10-3 record and earning a spot in the College Football Playoff. However, their season ended with a 34-24 loss to Alabama in the first round, and Oklahoma has struggled to find consistency this year. The potent offense Oklahoma showcased last season has largely been absent throughout the 2026 campaign. The exceptions came in the season opener against UTEP, when the Sooners cruised to a 51-0 victory, and this past weekend, when they defeated then-No. 1 Texas in the Red River Rivalry. However, not all 27 points against Texas came from the offense. Oklahoma scored a touchdown after blocking and recovering a punt in the end zone, while another touchdown came on a pick-six. The Sooners’ other scoring plays included a rushing touchdown and two field goals. Across their other three games, Oklahoma has averaged just 12.3 points per game, which is disappointing for an offense expected to be productive under quarterback John Mateer. Speaking of Mateer, he has completed 90 of 135 pass attempts for a 66.7% completion rate, totaling 1,038 passing yards, eight touchdowns, and four interceptions this season. Mateer is also a running threat, recording 53 carries for 70 rushing yards. Those numbers fall short of his previous two seasons in terms of passing production. In 2025, Mateer threw for 2,885 yards, while he recorded 3,139 passing yards in 2024. His touchdown-to-interception numbers also tell an interesting story. Mateer threw 14 touchdowns and 11 interceptions in 2025, compared with 29 touchdowns and seven interceptions in 2024. For Oklahoma to defeat Kentucky, the Sooners will need Mateer to take another step forward and help their offense become more consistent. For Kentucky to win in Norman, Kenny Minchey and the offense will have to find a way to pierce the Sooners’ stingy defense and avoid game-breaking turnovers that won Oklahoma the game vs. then-No. 1 Texas. As for other notable Oklahoma players, the receiving corps features wide receiver Isaiah Sategna III, Mateer’s primary target, along with tight end Rocky Beers and wide receiver Trell Harris. Kentucky will need to account for all three playmakers while also limiting the Sooners’ running game, which features Lloyd Avant and Jonathan Hatton Jr. Game: Kentucky Football vs. Oklahoma Sooners Location: Oklahoma Memorial Stadium — Norman, Oklahoma Date: Saturday, Oct. 17 Time: 7:30 p.m. ET TV Info: SEC Network will have the TV broadcast Online Streaming: WatchESPN Radio: UK Sports Network Opening Odds: FanDuel lists Kentucky as a 6.5-point underdog . ESPN gives Kentucky a 32.1% chance of winning. Our Early Prediction: Kentucky enters this matchup at 5-1 under first-year head coach Will Stein after a huge upset over LSU, while Oklahoma is coming off a rivalry win over Texas. Both teams could experience an emotional hangover after their big victories, but I believe Kentucky can overcome that challenge and earn another road win. Despite concerns about linebacker injuries, the Wildcats have a chance to improve to 6-1, become bowl-eligible, and remain in the College Football Playoff conversation. away.headline: Kentucky vs. Oklahoma Injury Report: Updates on CJ Baxter, Nic Anderson, and more
away.blurb: For Kentucky, the big news is that running back CJ Baxter is questionable to play this week. Baxter got dinged in the second half of the win over LSU but still finished the game and ran for a touchdown in overtime. He’s been one of the SEC’s best backs thus far, so not having him in Norman would be a major setback for this offense. Wide receiver Nic Anderson, who left last week’s win over LSU with a shoulder injury, is listed as probable, so he should be good to go this week as long as there are no setbacks. Defensive tackle Kalen Edwards, who missed last week, is questionable to play. As expected, linebacker Antwan Smith and cornerback Jaden Smith remain out after suffering injuries at South Carolina. Linebacker Tavion Wallace, out for the past two weeks, is still listed as out. Fellow linebacker Alex Afari Jr. is listed as questionable as he works through the legal process in hopes of regaining eligibility. He’s healthy, so if granted eligibility in the courts, he should play Saturday, but that’s a big if right now. Cornerback Grant Grayton remains out. Reserve defensive end Tyler Thomas is doubtful. Reserve tight end Elijah Brown is questionable. Finally, cornerback Hassan Sykes is probable to play. For Oklahoma, standout left tackle Michael Fasusi is nearing a return from a shoulder injury that has kept him out since Week 1. He’s currently listed as questionable. Starting left guard Eddy Pierre-Louis, who missed last week’s win over No. 1 Texas, is questionable. Backup lineman Fred Hinton is questionable as well. Cornerback Eli Bowen, who missed last week, is questionable to play. Fellow cornerback Jacobe Johnson, who was also out last week, is listed as out for this one. Wide receiver Parker Livingstone, who has six catches for 51 yards this year, is questionable. Running back Tory Blaylock, who has 10 carries for 22 yards, is probable. Tight end Jack Van Dorselaer, who does not have a catch this season, is probable. Finally, linebacker Taylor Heim, running back Xavier Robinson, tight end Trynae Washington, and wide receiver Trell Harris have been ruled out. away.headline: Oklahoma vs. Kentucky Injury Report: Sooners offensive line banged up
away.blurb: After initially being listed as questionable, Michael Fasusi and Heath Ozaeta, a pair of players who have started a number of games for the Sooners over the last two seasons, were downgraded to doubtful. They joined fellow offensive lineman Eddy Pierre-Louis as doubtful. This comes after Head coach Brent Venables said Fasusi was "just about ready" to make his return on Tuesday. Well, it looks like we'll have to wait another week for Fasusi's return. With Fasusi, Ozaeta, and Pierre-Louis doubtful for Saturday, the Sooners will have another combination starting up front for the Sooners. Ryan Fodje will continue to start at left tackle with true freshman Noah Best at left guard. Jake Miakkula will be at center once again with E'Marion Harris at right tackle. That leaves right guard as the question mark. Peyton Joseph is probably the player coming off the bench to start for the Sooners. He's been a rotational player at guard this season, playing 47 snaps this season. Starting cornerback Eli Bowen has been ruled out for Saturday, putting Trystan Haynes in line to make his second straight start. For the Kentucky Wildcats , one of the most important names to watch ahead of Saturday's primetime affair is running back C.J. Baxter. Baxter joined Kentucky via the transfer portal from Texas. He's run for 484 yards and eight touchdowns at 5.6 yards per carry this season. He remains questionable for Saturday, and Pete Nakos of On3 says he'll be a game-time decision. It would be a big blow to the Wildcats, but they have capable runners behind him on the depth chart in Jason Patterson (361 yards, 7.7 yards per carry) and former Sooner Jovantae Barnes (140 yards, 6.1 yards per carry). Fasusi has missed the last four games after playing with a shoulder injury against UTEP. Ozaeta was banged up in warm-ups ahead of the Red River Showdown, but still played 59 snaps up front. picks.blurb: Adam Carriker's Nebraska vs. Oregon Preview and Prediction Skip to main content SI.COM ALL THE GAMES ALUMNI GROUPS FOOTBALL SCHEDULE SI.COM HUSKERS FB BASKETBALL NEWS SI.COM HUSKERS BB Nebraska football is hitting the road for one of its biggest games of the season, and Adam Carriker is breaking it all down on the Carriker Chronicles! Matt Rhule and the Nebraska Cornhuskers are heading to Eugene to face Dan Lanning and the Oregon Ducks in a late-night Big Ten showdown. Both teams are coming off losses, and both have plenty to prove. Can the Huskers bounce back and pull off an upset? Nebraska enters the game at 5-1 after a heartbreaking loss to Curt Cignetti and Indiana. The Huskers showed some good things against the Hoosiers, but once again, they couldn't finish the job. Carriker discusses why Nebraska needs more than another moral victory. At some point, the Huskers have to start winning these big games, especially against talented Big Ten opponents. One of the biggest questions is whether Anthony Colandrea and Nebraska's offense can get things going against Oregon's defense. Colandrea has shown he can make plays, but Carriker believes offensive coordinator Dana Holgorsen needs to put him in good situations, especially on third downs. The Huskers also need production from Jamal Rule and the running back rotation. Can Nebraska establish a running game and keep Oregon's defense guessing? On the other side of the ball, Nebraska's Blackshirts face a major challenge. Oregon has talented receivers who can stretch the field and create explosive plays. Carriker looks at Nebraska's defensive numbers and explains why the Huskers cannot allow Oregon to make big plays over the top. The Blackshirts have been improving, but this will be another serious test of just how far they've come. Carriker also breaks down Oregon's defense, including players like Matayo Uiagalelei and Bear Alexander. The Ducks have plenty of talent, but Oregon has also been unpredictable this season. Nebraska cannot afford to let this become the game where everything suddenly clicks for Oregon. This is also Nebraska's stiffest road test so far this year. Playing in Eugene, in front of a loud Oregon crowd, will test the Huskers' experience and mental toughness. Nebraska has added veteran players who have been through big games before. Now it's time to see whether that experience pays off. Carriker shares his four keys to the game: handle Oregon's crowd, execute in the red zone, prevent big plays and play all four quarters. Nebraska must protect Colandrea, finish drives and avoid the mistakes that have cost the Huskers in close games. Finally, Carriker discusses the point spread and makes his score prediction! He's picking Nebraska to pull off the upset, 24-21! Can Matt Rhule and the Huskers shock Oregon, earn their third Big Ten win and make a statement to the rest of college football? Or will Dan Lanning and the Ducks send Nebraska home with another disappointing loss? Get Adam Carriker's full Nebraska-Oregon preview, breakdown and prediction on the Carriker Chronicles! Stay up to date on all things Huskers by bookmarking Nebraska Cornhuskers On SI , following us on Twitter/X , and visiting HuskerMax.com daily. Published Oct 14, 2026 ADAM CARRIKER Adam’s dream of playing for the Huskers came to fruition. He was twice named first-team All-Big 12, leading the conference in sacks and winning the Big 12 Defensive Lineman of the Year award his senior season, along with several other awards, including finishing with All-America honors, in addition to being named to the Big 12 Commissioner’s Academic Honor Roll three times. He’s also been named to Nebraska’s All-Century Team, voted The Best Husker Defensive End since the start of the new millennium, and has been inducted into the Nebraska Football Hall of Fame. Adam went on to play eight years as a Defensive Lineman in the NFL with the St. Louis Rams and Washington Redskins. He was drafted in the 1st round, winning Rams Rookie of the Year; he’s the only Ram in franchise history to start all 16 games as a rookie. He also won the Strongest Redskin award multiple times during his career in the NFL. Since retiring, he’s experienced great success in the business world and has also appeared multiple times on National Television and Radio Shows, and currently hosts his highly popular show, the Carriker Chronicles, aka, the People’s Show, which has been viewed by millions! Nebraska vs Oregon Odds Nebraska vs Oregon point spread : Oregon -6.5 (-118), Nebraska +6.5 (-104) Nebraska vs Oregon over/under : 51.5 (-110o / -110u) Nebraska vs Oregon moneyline : Nebraska +198, Oregon -245 One of the biggest storylines about the Nebraska season is how much better it got after Dylan Raiola left town. Anthony Colandrea has been a revelation since coming in from UNLV , completing 64% of his passes with an impressive 13:3 touchdown -to-interception ratio. Half of those passing scores went to Kwazi Gilmer, the UCLA transfer. Colandrea had a rough outing against Indiana , and for the most part, it seemed as if Nebraska was going to pull away. But in traditional Nebraska fashion, it ended up blowing it against the defending champs, losing 20-17. It was a rough outing for the Huskers' defense, a defense that has been really strong all season long. But Indiana scored on a one-play, 75-yard touchdown to Nick Marsh, which all but sealed the game for the Huskers. After that, the Hoosiers pulled away for good. Head coach Matt Rhule has developed a reputation at the college level that he can't win the big one. Last week proved that it's still true. The Huskers' run game should be used effectively, ranking 39th in Success Rate and third in explosiveness . Jamal Rule and Mekhi Nelson have split the carries, with Rule averaging 6.8 yards per carry and Nelson being more of a threat through the air. There's definitely a lot of talent on this defense, but they are prone to giving up big plays. Defensive back Dwayne McDougle has been a tackling machine and recorded an 81-yard pick-six. Nebraska's pass rush has also been really strong, generating Havoc on 18.5% of plays. DL Jahsear Whittington leads the team with 2.5 sacks and a forced fumble. Oregon has been one of the biggest disappointments this season. Coming into the season with championship hopes, it has now dropped two games in the first five games. The Ducks will continue to be without quarterback Dante Moore , and it may be Raiola getting the start against his old program, Nebraska. Raiola looked strong in relief against USC , completing 76% of his passes with a pair of touchdowns. However, when Oregon took on UCLA, Raiola was completely exposed, throwing two picks and only completing six out of 19 attempts. Ultimately, he was benched for Brock Thomas, a walk-on. It will hurt the Ducks this week, as they won't have wide receivers Jeremiah McClellan or Evan Stewart , which means Dakorien Moore will need to step up as more of a volume receiver. A big reason why this season has been brutal is because of Oregon's change of approach to the run. Last season, the Ducks averaged 36.6 rushing attempts per game, while this season, they average 28.8 attempts, which is 126th in the FBS. Jordon Davison and Dierre Hill Jr. have essentially split the carries, with Davison averaging just under five yards per carry. But they both have lacked the explosiveness needed to be truly effective. The run game may be ranked 62nd, but because Oregon doesn't run the ball as much, the offense has become very predictable. There are a ton of stars on this defense, including safety Koi Perich, who leads the team in solo tackles and two picks, as well as defensive tackle Matayo Uiagalelei, with five sacks. Overall, the Ducks have an impressive secondary, but the defense has been the clear definition of mediocre, so it's hard to take it seriously. I never thought, when looking at the schedule, of taking the Huskers to cover, but here we are. Oregon has been brutal when it comes to the spread, while the Huskers are 5-1. I'm typically not a believer in moral victories, but I think there's something to be said about how Nebraska had the Hoosiers on their heels for most of last week. The Huskers are better than their reputation says; it's really about closing games, which they still can't do. Needless to say, with the spread being a full touchdown, I don't think it's out of the question to pick Nebraska to cover. Whether it's Raiola or Thomas starting, I think this will end up being a positive for the Husker defense. Pick: Nebraska +6.5

Brown coming off IR ALCS Game 4 postponed Defense will win WNBA Finals Expert score prediction: Nebraska vs. Oregon Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Nebraska's loss to Indiana last week stung, with the team dropping a 17-6 lead to the defending national champion. Now the Huskers travel up to Oregon for a 10 p.m. CT matchup, the latest start time for Nebraska since 2014. But other factors in this game make this clash all the more questionable. Dante Moore is out for the game, meaning Dylan Raiola, Brock Thomas or even Akili Smith Jr. will be earning the start. But Raiola is the most poetic option after all and is likely the starter despite a rough outing against UCLA. After going 19-of-25 for 289 yards and two touchdowns against USC, Raiola only threw 6-of-19 for 43 yards and two interceptions against the Bruins . He also got strip-sacked in the game. Though it was Raiola's only sack, UCLA still brought the pressure throughout. Raiola's main weakness is pressure, which the Bruins exploited last week. Though Raiola can find ways to stay alive in the pocket and deliver big plays, he rarely takes off downfield and has found himself in rough spots. Thomas took over in the fourth quarter for the Ducks and went 11-of-15 for 156 yards and a touchdown. He did, however, fumble on his opening drive but nearly completed the comeback. But even if Thomas starts, it remains to be seen whether he can replicate that success, especially after seeing Raiola's two-game stretch. Now, Nebraska can get to the quarterback, but the concern comes down to the explosive plays. Indiana pulled off multiple explosive plays last week, despite its struggle to produce points and yardage for most of the game. The Ducks can do the same, especially late in the game. Nebraska ran out of steam in the fourth against Indiana at home early in the afternoon. Now, the Huskers face Oregon on the road after dark. The Ducks almost completed their 17-6 comeback against UCLA, so they can find a way to do the same against Nebraska if needed. The Huskers' defense also needs to be cautious with Oregon's rushing game. Though the Ducks don't strike primarily on the ground, Dierre Hill Jr. and Jordon Davison combined for 216 rushing yards and four touchdowns on 54 carries over the last two games, averaging four yards per carry. Though UCLA did suffocate Oregon's run at times, Nebraska could let a play slip by if it's not careful. Oregon's defense also needs to be cautious, seeing how its last two games panned out. The Ducks held USC to 27 points, but Jayden Maiava still threw for 326 yards and two touchdowns on just 23 completions. Oregon also surrendered 205 passing yards on just 13 completions to UCLA, despite holding it to 17 points. Nebraska could do some damage on the run, however. Oklahoma State's Drew Mestemaker tallied 109 rushing yards earlier this season against the Ducks. Anthony Colandrea could do the same and help the Huskers score. Jamal Rule, Mekhi Nelson and Isaiah Mozee all could have moments as well after UCLA's Wayne Knight found some holes in Oregon's defensive line. Knight finished with 103 yards on 22 carries. But this game is also make-or-break for Oregon's postseason hopes, especially with Ohio State and even Northwestern coming up. The Ducks also have a talented roster and, despite their issues, can deliver major blows to opponents when momentum is on their side. Nebraska's issues on the line, in the secondary and even a bit on special teams don't help either. All of this, plus the after-dark setting, provides just enough to tip the scales in the Ducks' favor. Unless Nebraska can truly come out and play like a team that can earn a top-25 spot, this matchup will likely be another so-close-but-so-far loss. away.headline: Oregon’s Dante Moore, Dylan Raiola, an Injury and a Brock Thomas QB Competition for Nebraska
away.blurb: But at Autzen Stadium, one QB is going to run out for the first offensive snap for the Ducks, and no matter who it is, it'll be a fascinating decision. Oregon’s Dante Moore, Dylan Raiola, an Injury and a Brock Thomas QB Competition for Nebraska - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF EUGENE, OREGON - SEPTEMBER 18: Dante Moore #5 of the Oregon Ducks looks to throw during the first half against the Portland State Vikings at Autzen Stadium on September 18, 2026 in Eugene, Oregon. (Photo by Soobum Im/Getty Images) Getty Billy Heyen Wed, October 14, 2026 at 8:21 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads The Oregon Ducks are home on Saturday night to host the Nebraska Cornhuskers. For those tuned in to these two teams, there are a lot of narratives at play — and many of them stem from the Ducks' QB depth chart of Dante Moore, Dylan Raiola and Brock Thomas. It's the kind of situation that may or may not get more clarity before kickoff on Saturday. Is Dante Moore Playing This Week? The intrigue starts with Moore, whose playing status for the game against Nebraska seems to remain uncertain. He hasn't played since being concussed against USC on a dirty hit after he slid to the turf. Raiola replaced him in that game, then the Ducks had a bye, and then Raiola started last week. Whether or not Moore will miss another game is a crucial factor one way or the other, but it doesn't seem decided. Is Dylan Raiola Starting This Week? The next factor at play is Raiola, who was pulled midway through Oregon's loss to UCLA. He was just 6-for-19 for 43 yards with two interceptions before head coach Dan Lanning pulled him in the fourth quarter. Lanning told reporters at the start of this week that if Moore can't go on Saturday, that will bring about a QB competition in practice for who starts against the Cornhuskers. Of course, Raiola would love to face Nebraska. That's the school he played at for two years after being the No. 1 quarterback recruit in the country. Then he transferred to Oregon in the offseason, and it seemed he'd just be the backup when the Ducks played the Cornhuskers — but now there's at least a chance he starts. Thomas began the year as Oregon's third quarterback, but he went 11-for-15 for 156 yards and a touchdown in an attempted comeback against UCLA. He's not the high-pedigree recruit of the Ducks' other two quarterbacks, but sometimes productivity gets rewarded. Thomas is actually a cool story, because he's from Eugene and played locally at Sheldon High School. He played in a state title game in high school and also won a 4×100-meter relay state title on the track. A three-star recruit, Thomas picked the hometown team as a third-generation Ducks player — his grandfather Paul Bauge and father Aaron Thomas both played at Oregon, too. home.headline: What we're hearing on Oregon injuries ahead of Nebraska
home.blurb: However, it doesn't appear that things are going to get any easier, with the Nebraska Cornhuskers coming to town, and starting quarterback Dante Moore once again ruled out after the concussion he suffered in Week 4 against the USC Trojans . That will leave either Brock Thomas, Dylan Raiola, or Akili Smith Jr. under center with the start, and a big onus on the offense to show some improvement. While the Big Ten Availability report was released on Wednesday and will again come out on Thursday and Friday nights, we've got some intel on where things stand with each injured player and whether or not they will be able to contribute this weekend. Here's our early look at who we think could potentially be out or limited in this game on Friday night. There was some hope that Dante Moore might be able to give it a go this week after returning to practice following his concussion, but the fact that he was ruled "out" in the first availability report, and not even "questionable," is not a great sign for an expedient return. We will see if Moore is able to go next week against Illinois, but it could still be a couple of weeks before we see No. 5 back on the field, if at all. McClellan has been out for a few weeks now after suffering a broken foot in warmups before the Portland State game, and has been seen wearing a walking boot during games. We will see when he is able to get out of the boot and back to practice, but it might still be several weeks, at the least. "He's going to be done for the foreseeable future. (It's) something he tried to tough out. You know, credit to him. Sometimes you can play through that, but you're probably not going to play as well. But it's one of those ones where it made sense to get it repaired for him." According to head coach Dan Lanning, Platt is still dealing with an undisclosed injury that held him out of the spring game earlier this year. Oregon's coach does not expect him to return to the field anytime soon. "He's gonna be limited for a while with the injury he felt in the spring," Lanning said of Platt. "I don't want to put a timeline on it, but he's going to be out for some time until we see where he's at and continue to progress and challenge himself." After suffering a neck injury during fall camp a year ago, Gresham was held out for the entire 2025 season and has yet to return to the field. Oregon still has him on the roster, but it doesn't sound like he will be back anytime soon. After starting the game against Oklahoma State, Ferguson was forced to the sideline in the first half with a knee injury that Dan Lanning says is expected to hold him out for the remainder of the season. Colorado transfer RB Simeon Price is yet to play this year and has been seen in street clothes wearing a walking boot recently during Oregon games.
